adhesive-dressings.description: Adhesive dressings combine an absorbent pad with an adhesive backing so they stay in place without extra tape. They range from small strips for minor cuts and cannula sites to larger island dressings, where a central pad is surrounded by an adhesive border, for surgical incisions. Backings may be woven fabric, plastic film or non-woven material, and many pads have a low-adherent surface that lifts cleanly from the wound. Choose a size where the pad fully covers the wound and the adhesive sits on healthy skin, with gentler adhesives for fragile skin.

aeds.description: Automated external defibrillators (AEDs) analyse the heart rhythm through adhesive chest pads and advise or deliver a shock when a shockable rhythm such as ventricular fibrillation is detected. Voice and visual prompts guide the rescuer through pad placement, CPR and shock delivery, so trained laypersons and first responders can act before a clinical team arrives. Semi-automatic models ask the user to press a shock button, fully automatic models shock without input, and protocols use fixed or escalating energy. Plan for pad and battery expiry and a visible, accessible wall cabinet.

airway-kits.description: Airway kits gather the devices needed to open, secure and ventilate an airway into one pack, so essentials are ready at the bedside, on resuscitation trolleys or in transport bags. Typical contents include oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal airways in several sizes, a bag-valve-mask, face masks, endotracheal tubes with stylet and syringe, a tube holder and lubricant, and some kits add a laryngoscope. Components are individually sterile-packed where required, and adult and paediatric configurations are available. Kits should be checked on a set schedule for completeness, expiry dates and, where included, laryngoscope light function.
airway-kits.specifications: Typical contents: OPA/NPA airways, BVM, face masks, ETTs, stylet, syringe, tube holder, lubricant; Optional: laryngoscope handle and blades; Configurations: adult, paediatric; Packaging: individually sterile-packed components in pouch or case; Use: single-use consumables

alcohol-preparations.description: Alcohol preparations are isopropyl or ethyl alcohol products, commonly around 70 percent, used for skin antisepsis before injections and venepuncture and for wiping injection ports, vial stoppers and small equipment. Single-use formats include individually sealed prep pads, swabs and sachets, while bulk bottles from 500 mL to 5 L are used for general antisepsis and wiping. Sterile swab variants are available for procedures that require them. Alcohol acts quickly but evaporates fast and leaves no lasting effect, so allow the skin to dry fully before puncture, and keep containers closed and away from flames.
alcohol-preparations.specifications: Active: isopropyl or ethyl alcohol, typically 70%; Formats: prep pads, swabs, sachets, bottles; Pad material: nonwoven, single or multi-ply; Pack sizes: single sachets to 500 mL–5 L; Sterility: non-sterile, sterile swab variants available

alcohol-swabs.description: Alcohol swabs are small, individually wrapped pads saturated with isopropyl alcohol, typically around 70%, used to clean skin before injections and venepuncture and to disinfect vial tops, injection ports and small equipment surfaces. Each sealed packet keeps the pad moist until opened. Allow the alcohol to dry on the skin for full effect and to reduce stinging. Alcohol swabs are not intended for open wounds, and some procedures, such as blood cultures or central line care, may call for chlorhexidine-alcohol preparations instead.
alcohol-swabs.specifications: Solution: about 65–70% isopropyl alcohol; Pad: non-woven fabric; Packaging: individually sealed sachets; Sterility: sterile; Use: single use

alginate-dressings.description: Alginate dressings are made from calcium or calcium-sodium alginate fibres derived from seaweed. When they absorb wound fluid they turn into a soft gel, which makes them suitable for moderately to heavily exuding wounds, cavities and wounds with minor bleeding, since released calcium supports clotting. Flat pads cover surface wounds, while ribbon or rope forms loosely pack sinuses and cavity wounds. Alginates need a secondary dressing to hold them in place and are not recommended for dry wounds, because they rely on exudate to form a gel.

ambu-bags.description: Ambu bags, also called bag-valve-mask resuscitators, are hand-squeezed self-inflating bags used to ventilate patients who are not breathing or are breathing inadequately, during CPR, before intubation and in transport. A set typically includes the bag, a non-rebreathing patient valve, a face mask and an oxygen reservoir, with a pressure-relief valve common on paediatric and neonatal sizes. Reusable silicone versions are reprocessed between patients, while single-patient-use versions are also widely used. Choose bag volume by patient size, add a PEEP valve when needed, and squeeze only enough to make the chest rise, avoiding over-ventilation.
ambu-bags.specifications: Bag volume: approx. 1,500–2,000 mL adult, 500–700 mL paediatric, 200–300 mL infant/neonate; Material: silicone (reusable) or PVC/plastic (single-use); Components: patient valve, face mask, O2 reservoir and tubing; Valves: pressure relief, optional PEEP valve; Connector: standard 15/22 mm

aneroid-sphygmomanometers.description: Aneroid sphygmomanometers are manual blood pressure devices made up of an inflatable cuff, a hand bulb with release valve and a mechanical dial gauge, with readings taken by listening for Korotkoff sounds through a stethoscope. Being mercury-free and needing no power, they are used in outpatient clinics, wards and outreach work, and where automated readings may be unreliable, such as in irregular heart rhythms. Palm-held, desk and clip-on gauges are available with adult, large adult and paediatric cuffs. The needle should rest at zero before inflation, and gauges should be checked regularly, as they can drift, especially after being dropped.

applicators.description: Applicators are thin sticks tipped with absorbent cotton, used to apply ointments and antiseptics, clean small or hard-to-reach areas such as wound edges, ears, nostrils and stoma sites, and perform delicate cleaning. Wooden or plastic shafts come in single-ended and double-ended versions. Sterile individually wrapped applicators suit wound care and procedures, while non-sterile bulk packs serve general tasks. For microbiology specimens, use dedicated collection swabs, since standard cotton tips and wooden shafts can affect some laboratory tests.
applicators.specifications: Tip: cotton, single or double-ended; Shaft: wood or plastic; Length: standard about 15cm; Packaging: sterile individually wrapped or non-sterile bulk; Use: single use

autoclaves.description: Autoclaves are pressurized chambers that sterilize reusable instruments, glassware, linen and media with saturated steam, typically at about 121°C or 134°C for a validated exposure time. They range from 10-litre benchtop units for dental and outpatient clinics to 100-litre-plus units for operating theatres, CSSD and laboratories. Gravity-displacement models suit solid, unwrapped items and liquids, while pre-vacuum models actively remove air and are needed for wrapped packs, porous loads and hollow instruments. When choosing, match chamber size and cycle types to your usual loads, and plan for routine indicator testing and the water quality the unit requires.

automated-dispensing-cabinets.description: Automated dispensing cabinets are computer-controlled medication storage units on wards or in pharmacies that release medicines only to authorised users and record every transaction. Staff log in by password, card or fingerprint, select a patient and medicine, and the cabinet unlocks only the drawer, pocket or lidded compartment holding it. This supports controlled-drug security, real-time stock tracking, restocking reports and fewer selection errors, with drawer layouts ranging from open matrix drawers to single-dose locked pockets. Integration with pharmacy and ordering systems is a key consideration, along with network, backup power and staff training.
automated-dispensing-cabinets.specifications: Storage: matrix drawers, lidded pockets, locked towers; Access: password, ID card or biometric; Software: transaction logging and inventory reports; Integration: pharmacy and ordering system interface; Options: refrigerated compartment, auxiliary cabinets

beard-covers.description: Beard covers are disposable nonwoven covers that enclose facial hair on the chin, jaw and lower cheeks, held in place by elastic loops over the ears or around the head. They are worn in operating theatres, sterile compounding areas, CSSD packing rooms, laboratories and hospital kitchens to keep hair from falling onto sterile items, specimens or food. Worn together with a cap or bouffant, they complete head and facial hair coverage. Beard covers do not provide respiratory protection, and wearers who need a respirator should note that facial hair under the seal prevents a proper fit.
beard-covers.specifications: Material: spunbond PP nonwoven; Fastening: elastic ear loops or head band; Coverage: chin, jaw and lower cheeks; Size: one size; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use

biohazard-waste-bins.description: Biohazard waste bins are lidded collection bins for infectious clinical waste such as contaminated dressings, gloves and disposable items, lined with colour-coded disposable bags. Common capacities range from about 20 L to 120 L, and foot-pedal or sensor lids allow hands-free opening to reduce contamination. Bins are typically made of durable, wipe-clean plastic or steel and display the biohazard symbol. The bin itself is reusable and should be cleaned regularly, while liners are tied off and removed before overfilling. Place bins where infectious waste is generated and match colours to the local segregation scheme.

biological-indicators.description: Biological indicators are test devices containing a known population of highly resistant bacterial spores, used to confirm that a sterilization cycle actually kills microorganisms. After processing in the most challenging location of a load, the indicator is incubated: no growth shows the cycle was lethal, while growth signals a failure to investigate. Self-contained vials holding spores and growth medium together are common, alongside spore strips. Steam and hydrogen peroxide indicators typically use Geobacillus stearothermophilus, while ethylene oxide and dry heat use Bacillus atrophaeus. An unprocessed control from the same lot should be incubated with each test.
biological-indicators.specifications: Organism: G. stearothermophilus (steam, H2O2) or B. atrophaeus (EO, dry heat); Spore population: typically approx. 10^5–10^6; Format: self-contained vial or spore strip; Incubation: approx. 55–60°C or 35–37°C by organism; Readout: colour change or fluorescence, rapid to 24–48 h

biopsy-forceps.description: Endoscopic biopsy forceps are flexible instruments passed through an endoscope's working channel to take small mucosal tissue samples for histology. They consist of a coiled sheath, a pair of opening cups at the tip and a handle that opens and closes the jaws. Variants include standard and jumbo cups, fenestrated jaws, smooth or serrated edges and an optional central needle that anchors the forceps on tangential tissue. Choose shaft length to suit gastroscope or colonoscope use and match outer diameter to the scope's channel; jumbo cups need a larger therapeutic channel.
biopsy-forceps.specifications: Cup type: standard or jumbo, oval or alligator; Jaw options: fenestrated, serrated, with or without needle; Outer diameter: approx. 1.8–2.8 mm; Working length: approx. 1600–2300 mm; Min. channel: approx. 2.0–3.2 mm

bipap-machines.description: BiPAP machines, or bilevel positive airway pressure devices, deliver two pressures: a higher inspiratory pressure (IPAP) to assist each breath and a lower expiratory pressure (EPAP) to keep the airway open. This suits them to non-invasive ventilation in conditions such as COPD exacerbations, hypercapnic respiratory failure, neuromuscular disease and sleep apnoea not tolerated on CPAP. Pressures typically span about 4 to 25 cmH2O, with spontaneous, timed and spontaneous/timed modes providing a backup breath rate. Hospital units add alarms and monitoring; a well-fitted full-face or nasal mask is essential, as leaks reduce effective support.

bipolar-electrosurgical-units.description: Bipolar electrosurgical units pass current only between the two tips of a bipolar forceps, so energy stays confined to the tissue held in the jaws and no patient return pad is needed. This gives precise, low-power coagulation for delicate work in neurosurgery, ophthalmic, ENT, hand and microsurgery, and near nerves or implanted devices. Power output is adjustable and usually far lower than monopolar settings. Units may be activated by footswitch or by auto-bipolar tissue sensing, and some support irrigating forceps that reduce tissue sticking to the tips.
bipolar-electrosurgical-units.specifications: Output: bipolar coagulation, some models with bipolar cut; Power: adjustable low-power output; Activation: footswitch or auto-bipolar sensing; Return pad: not required; Accessories: bipolar forceps and cables, irrigating forceps optional

blood-bank-refrigerators.description: Blood bank refrigerators store whole blood and red cell units within a tightly controlled 2–6°C range. Forced-air circulation keeps temperature uniform across shelves or drawers, and digital controllers with chart recorders or data logging record conditions for quality records. Audible and visual alarms warn of high or low temperature, door ajar and power failure, often with battery backup for the alarm system. Capacities typically range from about 100L to 700L, with glass or solid doors. Size the unit by the number of blood units held and check remote alarm options.

blood-collection-needles.description: Blood collection needles are designed for venepuncture, either as double-ended needles that screw into a tube holder for evacuated tube systems, or as winged butterfly sets with flexible tubing for small, fragile or hard-to-reach veins. Gauges of 21G to 23G balance sample flow against patient comfort, with 21G common for routine adult draws and 23G for children and difficult veins. Many include a safety shield that covers the needle after use. Confirm compatibility with the tube holders and tubes in use, and use a discard tube with butterfly sets when coagulation tubes are drawn first.
blood-collection-needles.specifications: Types: multi-sample double-ended, winged butterfly set; Gauges: 21G, 22G, 23G; Safety: with or without needle shield; Compatibility: standard evacuated tube holders; Packaging: sterile, single use

blood-glucose-meters.description: Blood glucose meters are handheld devices that measure glucose in a small drop of capillary blood applied to a disposable test strip, giving a result within seconds. In hospitals and clinics they are used for point-of-care monitoring of patients with diabetes, during insulin infusions and for screening, and they are also used for home self-monitoring. Most strips use an enzyme-based electrochemical method needing only about 0.3 to 1 microlitre of blood, obtained with a sterile single-use lancet. Use strips matched to the meter, check their expiry dates and run control solutions regularly, since hematocrit and some substances can affect results.
blood-glucose-meters.specifications: Method: electrochemical, glucose oxidase or dehydrogenase strips; Sample: approx. 0.3–1 µL capillary whole blood; Measuring range: approx. 20–600 mg/dL (1.1–33.3 mmol/L); Test time: approx. 5–10 s; Consumables: test strips, sterile lancets, control solution

blood-pressure-monitors.description: Blood pressure monitors measure arterial blood pressure non-invasively with an inflatable cuff around the upper arm, either automatically by oscillometric sensing or manually with a gauge and stethoscope. In hospitals they are used for routine vital signs on wards, spot checks in outpatient clinics, triage in emergency departments and scheduled repeat readings in critical care. Options include portable desktop units, units on mobile stands and devices that also record pulse rate and store readings. Accurate results depend heavily on the correct cuff, so keep adult, large adult and paediatric cuffs available and choose by measured arm circumference.

boot-covers.description: Boot covers are disposable, calf- or knee-length overshoes that cover footwear and the lower leg, giving more protection than standard shoe covers when floors may be wet with blood, irrigation fluid or other contaminated liquids. They are used in operating rooms, delivery suites, autopsy rooms and isolation areas and during spill clean-up, and are often worn with coveralls. Most are polypropylene nonwoven or film-coated fabric with ties or elastic at the top, and many have a non-slip sole. Choose fluid-resistant coated versions for wet procedures and check that the top closure stays up during movement.
boot-covers.specifications: Material: PP nonwoven, SMS or PE-coated/laminated; Height: calf to knee length; Top closure: ties or elastic; Sole: non-slip on many models; Size: one size, XL; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use

bouffant-caps.description: Bouffant caps are loose, gathered disposable head covers with an elastic edge, designed to contain all of the hair, including long or thick hair, so that hair and skin flakes do not shed into clean areas. Made from lightweight, breathable polypropylene nonwoven, they are worn in operating rooms, CSSD, pharmacy compounding areas, laboratories and food service. The roomy, pleated shape suits staff with long hair or buns that a fitted surgical cap would not fully cover. They come in one size and should be pulled down to cover the ears and hairline.
bouffant-caps.specifications: Material: spunbond PP nonwoven; Fabric weight: approx. 10–20 gsm; Diameter: approx. 18–24 in (46–61 cm) flat; Edge: elasticated; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use

c-arms.description: C-arms are mobile fluoroscopy systems with an X-ray source and image receptor mounted at opposite ends of a C-shaped arm, providing real-time imaging during surgery and interventional procedures. They are widely used in orthopaedic and trauma theatres, pain management, urology and vascular work, where the arm rotates around the patient without moving them. Systems use either an image intensifier or a flat-panel detector, with a separate monitor cart for live and stored images. The arm is covered with sterile drapes in theatre; consider detector size, rotation range, dose-reduction features and manoeuvring space.
c-arms.specifications: Detector: image intensifier (approx. 9–12 in) or flat panel; Imaging: continuous and pulsed fluoroscopy, spot images; Movement: orbital and angular rotation; Display: monitor cart with image storage; Drapes: sterile covers for OR use

canes.description: Walking canes are single-handed mobility aids that improve balance and offload some weight from a weaker leg, for people who need less support than crutches or a walking frame. Single-point canes are light and suit mild balance problems, while tripod and quad canes have a broader base that stands on its own and gives more stability, often used after a stroke. Most are height-adjustable aluminium with offset or crook handles. A cane is usually held in the hand opposite the affected leg with the handle at about wrist height, and worn rubber tips should be replaced.
canes.specifications: Types: single-point, tripod, quad base; Material: aluminium (adjustable); Height: push-button adjustment; Handle: crook, offset or ergonomic grip; Tip: non-slip rubber ferrule; Quad base: small or large

capnography-monitors.description: Capnography monitors measure carbon dioxide in exhaled breath and display it as an end-tidal CO2 value and a continuous waveform, giving breath-by-breath information on ventilation. They are used to confirm endotracheal tube placement, monitor ventilated patients and those under procedural sedation, and assess the effectiveness of CPR. Mainstream sensors sit directly in the airway circuit of intubated patients, while sidestream units draw a small gas sample through a disposable line, which also allows monitoring through nasal sampling cannulas in non-intubated patients. Sampling lines and airway adapters must match the monitor and patient size.
capnography-monitors.specifications: Measurement: EtCO2, respiratory rate, CO2 waveform; Technology: non-dispersive infrared; Sampling: mainstream or sidestream (approx. 50–200 mL/min); EtCO2 range: typically 0–99 mmHg or wider; Consumables: airway adapters, sampling lines, nasal CO2 cannulas

central-monitoring-systems.description: Central monitoring systems bring the waveforms, vital signs and alarms from many bedside monitors onto screens at a nursing station, so staff can observe several patients at once in ICUs, high-dependency units and step-down wards. They usually run on a workstation with one or more large displays connected to bedside and telemetry monitors over a wired or wireless network. Typical functions include full-disclosure review, trend and event storage, central alarm handling and printing or export to electronic records. Choose a system compatible with your existing bedside monitors and sized for the number of beds and data retention you need.
central-monitoring-systems.specifications: Capacity: multiple beds per station, model-dependent; Display: one or more large screens, multi-patient layout; Connectivity: wired LAN or wireless, bedside and telemetry monitors; Functions: central alarms, trends, full-disclosure review; Data: storage, printing, EMR interface on many models

cervical-collars.description: Cervical collars support the neck and limit movement of the cervical spine when a spinal injury is suspected. Rigid extrication collars used in emergency care come in fixed sizes, from no-neck and short to regular, tall and paediatric, or as one adjustable collar that sets to several heights. Most have a front opening for pulse checks and airway access. Soft foam collars give comfort rather than true immobilisation. Size by measuring the neck carefully, since a poorly fitted collar may not restrict movement and can compromise the airway.
cervical-collars.specifications: Types: rigid extrication, adjustable, soft foam; Sizes: no-neck, short, regular, tall, paediatric or adjustable; Material: polyethylene shell with foam padding; Closure: hook-and-loop strap; Features: front tracheal access opening

chemical-indicators.description: Chemical indicators are strips, tapes, labels and inserts printed with ink that changes colour or form when exposed to sterilization conditions, giving a quick visual check that a pack or load has been processed. They are grouped into classes, from simple process indicators such as autoclave tape (Class 1) that separate processed from unprocessed items, through Bowie-Dick air-removal test sheets (Class 2), to integrating and emulating indicators (Classes 5 and 6) placed inside packs that respond to time, temperature and sterilant together. A passed indicator supports but does not prove sterility, so results are read alongside physical and biological monitoring.
chemical-indicators.specifications: Formats: indicator tape, strips, labels, Bowie-Dick test sheets; Classes: Class 1 process to Class 6 emulating; Processes: steam, EO, dry heat or hydrogen peroxide (method-specific); Readout: colour change or moving ink bar; Use: single-use, inside and/or outside packs

chemistry-analyzers.description: Chemistry analyzers are laboratory instruments that measure substances in serum, plasma or urine, such as glucose, lipids, kidney and liver function markers, electrolytes and enzymes. They mix sample and reagent, incubate the reaction and read it photometrically, and some add ion-selective electrodes for sodium, potassium and chloride. Semi-automated benchtop models suit smaller laboratories, while fully automated systems handle larger test menus and higher throughput with walk-away operation. Selection depends on daily test volume, the test menu needed, reagent availability, open versus closed reagent systems, and water, power and maintenance requirements.
chemistry-analyzers.specifications: Type: semi-automated or fully automated; Method: photometric, optional ISE for Na/K/Cl; Sample types: serum, plasma, urine; Throughput: low to several hundred tests per hour, model-dependent; Reagents: open or closed system; Data: LIS connectivity

chemotherapy-gloves.description: Chemotherapy gloves are disposable gloves tested for resistance to permeation by cytotoxic and other hazardous drugs, giving staff a barrier when preparing, administering or disposing of chemotherapy agents and handling contaminated waste or patient excreta. They are usually nitrile or another synthetic rubber, thicker than standard exam gloves, with extended cuffs that can be pulled over a gown sleeve. Non-sterile versions suit drug administration and spill clean-up, while sterile variants are used inside pharmacy compounding cabinets. Double gloving, and changing gloves at set intervals or after any tear or contamination, is standard practice when handling hazardous drugs.

clinical-waste-bags.description: Clinical waste bags are colour-coded disposable liners that contain infectious and other healthcare waste for collection, storage and treatment. Yellow is commonly used for infectious waste, with other colours assigned under local segregation rules, and bags often carry the biohazard symbol. Typical capacities of 20 L, 50 L, 80 L and 120 L fit standard bins and trolleys. Bag thickness and tear resistance matter for heavy or wet loads; bags should be filled to no more than about three-quarters, securely tied or sealed, and labelled with their source for traceability.

cohesive-bandages.description: Cohesive bandages stick to themselves but not to skin, hair or clothing, so they stay in place without clips, pins or tape. Made from a lightly coated non-woven or knitted material, they are used to secure dressings, IV lines and splints, give light compression and wrap sports injuries, and they tear easily by hand. Widths from 2.5cm for fingers to 10cm for limbs are common, often in several colours, with latex-free versions available. Because layers grip each other, apply with only moderate stretch to avoid excess pressure.

colonoscopes.description: Colonoscopes are long, forward-viewing flexible endoscopes used to examine the colon and terminal ileum for screening, diagnosis and therapy such as polypectomy. Adult instruments are typically about 12–13 mm in diameter with a working length of roughly 1600–1700 mm, and many offer adjustable insertion-tube stiffness to help navigate bowel loops. Paediatric colonoscopes have a smaller diameter for children or patients with a narrow or angulated colon. Working channel size matters when planning accessories, as larger channels accept bigger snares and clips and improve suction of fluid and debris.
colonoscopes.specifications: Insertion tube: approx. 12–13 mm (paediatric smaller); Working length: approx. 1600–1700 mm (shorter variants exist); Working channel: approx. 3.2–3.8 mm; Stiffness: fixed or variable; View: forward-viewing, wide angle; Reprocessing: high-level disinfection

colposcopes.description: Colposcopes are stand-mounted magnifiers used to examine the cervix, vagina and vulva in detail, typically after an abnormal cervical screening result. They provide illuminated magnification of about 6x to 40x from a working distance outside the patient, and a green filter highlights vessel patterns after acetic acid is applied. Optical models use binocular eyepieces, while video colposcopes display and record images on a monitor for documentation and teaching. Consider magnification steps, light source, fixed or mobile stand and image-capture needs, along with how the unit fits into biopsy and treatment workflows.
colposcopes.specifications: Magnification: approx. 6x–40x; Working distance: approx. 300 mm; Light source: LED or halogen; Filter: green (red-free); Mounting: fixed or mobile stand; Imaging: optical binocular or video

compression-bandages.description: Compression bandages apply sustained, graduated pressure to the lower leg to improve venous return and reduce swelling, and are central to managing venous leg ulcers and lymphoedema under clinical direction. Multi-layer systems combine padding, compression and cohesive outer layers to hold consistent pressure for several days, while short-stretch bandages give high working pressure during walking. Correct application requires training and an assessment of arterial circulation, such as an ankle-brachial pressure index, before use. Select the system by ankle circumference and the prescribed pressure level.

cotton-balls.description: Cotton balls are small balls of absorbent cotton wool used to clean skin, apply antiseptics and solutions, remove adhesive residue and apply pressure after injections and blood draws. They come in small, medium and large sizes, typically in packs of 100 to 500. Non-sterile balls suit general cleaning and skin care, while sterile packs are used in wound care and procedures. Cotton absorbs liquids readily but can leave loose fibres, so gauze or non-woven swabs may be preferred in open wounds.
cotton-balls.specifications: Material: absorbent bleached cotton; Sizes: small, medium, large; Pack size: 100–500 per bag; Sterility: non-sterile, sterile packs available; Use: single use

cotton-rolls.description: Cotton rolls are long rolls of absorbent cotton wool, commonly supplied as 500g rolls, that staff tear or cut to size for cleaning, padding and dressing. They are used to make cotton balls and swabs on the ward, to pad splints, casts and bony prominences, and to absorb fluids. Rolls are often interleaved with paper to keep layers separate and are available in different widths. Store them in a clean, dry, covered container and handle with clean hands, since an opened roll is non-sterile and exposed to repeated handling.
cotton-rolls.specifications: Material: absorbent bleached cotton; Weight: 500g rolls; Widths: various; Interleaving: commonly paper-interleaved; Sterility: non-sterile

coveralls.description: Coveralls are one-piece protective suits covering the torso, arms and legs, often with an attached hood, worn when more coverage than a gown is needed, such as caring for patients with highly infectious diseases, handling hazardous spills or decontamination work. They are made from microporous film-laminated nonwoven, SMS or similar fabrics, with elasticated hood, wrists and ankles and a front zip under a storm flap. These are disposable and come in S to XXL. Choose a size with room for bending and reaching, and plan a supervised removal sequence, since taking off a coverall without self-contamination takes practice.
coveralls.specifications: Material: microporous film-laminated PP or SMS nonwoven; Hood: attached, elasticated; Closure: front zip with storm flap; Cuffs/ankles: elasticated; Seams: stitched, bound or taped; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use

cpap-machines.description: CPAP machines deliver continuous positive airway pressure through a mask to keep the upper airway open, and are mainly used to treat obstructive sleep apnoea in sleep clinics and at home, with some use in hospital respiratory care. Fixed-pressure devices hold one prescribed pressure, while auto-titrating models adjust within a set range, typically 4–20 cmH2O, as breathing changes. Most offer ramp settings, heated humidification and recording of usage and leak data. Mask fit strongly affects comfort and adherence, so nasal, nasal pillow and full-face options should be available, with tubing and cushions cleaned and replaced regularly.

cpr-boards.description: CPR boards are rigid backboards placed under a patient lying on a soft bed or mattress so chest compressions push on the chest rather than sinking into the mattress. Half-body boards fit beneath the torso and slide in quickly during an in-hospital arrest, while full-body boards also support the head and pelvis. They are usually moulded plastic or composite with handgrips, and are often mounted on the back of a crash cart. Look for a lightweight, X-ray translucent board that is easy to wipe down and disinfect.
cpr-boards.specifications: Types: half-body and full-body; Material: moulded plastic or composite; Features: handholds, radiolucent options; Mounting: brackets for crash carts or walls; Cleaning: wipe-clean, disinfectant compatible

crepe-bandages.description: Crepe bandages are woven cotton bandages, sometimes blended with a small proportion of synthetic fibre, whose stretch comes from a crinkled crepe weave of twisted yarns rather than rubber threads. They give lighter support than high-stretch elastic bandages and are commonly used to retain dressings, support minor sprains and reduce swelling after soft-tissue injuries. Widths of 5cm, 7.5cm, 10cm and 15cm suit fingers and wrists through to knees and thighs. Crepe is breathable and can be washed and reused, though it gradually loses stretch.

crutches.description: Crutches transfer part of the body's weight from the legs to the arms, allowing patients to walk with reduced or no weight-bearing through an injured leg. Axillary (underarm) crutches give more support and are often used short-term after injury or surgery, while forearm (elbow) crutches with cuffs suit longer-term users but need more upper-body strength and coordination. Both are height-adjustable and come in paediatric to adult sizes. Correct fitting matters: axillary crutch tops should sit a few finger-widths below the armpit to avoid nerve pressure, and handgrips should allow a slight elbow bend.
crutches.specifications: Types: axillary and forearm/elbow; Frame: aluminium; Adjustment: push-button height adjustment; Sizes: paediatric, adult, tall; Tips: non-slip rubber ferrules; Padding: underarm pads and handgrips

cut-resistant-medical-gloves.description: Cut-resistant medical gloves are reusable knitted gloves made from high-performance fibres such as high-molecular-weight polyethylene, aramid or steel-reinforced yarns that resist slicing from blades and sharp edges. In hospitals and laboratories they are used during manual instrument cleaning and reprocessing, autopsy and pathology work, tissue grossing and handling broken glassware. They are non-sterile and come in S to XL. They resist cuts but give limited protection against needle punctures and none against fluids, so they are usually combined with a disposable glove, and should be laundered or decontaminated according to the manufacturer's instructions.

defibrillators.description: Defibrillators deliver a controlled electric shock to the heart to treat life-threatening rhythms such as ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia. Hospital units usually combine a manual mode, where the clinician reads the ECG and selects energy, with an AED mode, and many add synchronised cardioversion, transcutaneous pacing and ECG monitoring. Energy is typically selectable from about 1J to 360J, with biphasic waveforms now common, delivered through paddles or disposable adhesive pads. Check pacing capability, battery type, event recording and paediatric pad availability.

delivery-beds.description: Delivery beds, or birthing beds, are adjustable beds that support the mother through labour, delivery and recovery without transfer between surfaces. They usually have a retractable or removable foot section that opens access for delivery, plus leg supports or stirrups, hand grips and an adjustable backrest for different birthing positions. Electric or hydraulic models add height adjustment and Trendelenburg tilt for emergencies. Look for fluid-resistant, easy-clean upholstery, a catch basin or drainage tray, lockable castors and a mattress that can be reconfigured quickly when urgent intervention is needed.
delivery-beds.specifications: Adjustment: manual, hydraulic or electric; Positions: backrest, height, Trendelenburg; Foot section: retractable or removable; Supports: leg rests or stirrups, hand grips; Mattress: fluid-resistant, sectional; Mobility: castors with brakes

delivery-kits.description: Delivery kits are sterile, single-use packs that gather the basic items needed for a normal vaginal birth, helping teams prepare quickly and maintain a clean field. A typical kit includes umbilical cord clamps, cord-cutting scissors, drapes, an under-buttocks sheet and gauze swabs, and some add gloves, a kidney dish or a mucus extractor. Contents vary between kits, so facilities should check the component list against their delivery protocol and decide whether episiotomy or suturing items are needed separately. Packs are opened at the point of care and all components discarded after one delivery.
delivery-kits.specifications: Contents: cord clamps, scissors, drapes, gauze swabs; Optional items: gloves, under-buttocks drape, mucus extractor; Packaging: sterile, single-use pack; Use: one normal vaginal delivery

dental-autoclaves.description: Dental autoclaves are benchtop steam sterilisers used to sterilise handpieces, instruments and other reusable items in dental clinics. Chamber capacities are usually about 8 L to 23 L, and cycles typically run at around 121°C or 134°C depending on the load. Pre-vacuum models remove air from hollow and wrapped loads such as handpieces and pouched instruments, while simpler gravity cycles suit only unwrapped solid instruments. Cycle printing or data logging, a drying phase and water quality are practical considerations, and routine tests are needed to confirm the steriliser is performing correctly.

dental-chairs.description: Dental chairs are electrically adjustable patient chairs that position patients for examination and treatment so the dentist and assistant can reach the mouth comfortably. Motors control seat height, backrest recline and headrest position, often with programmable memory positions and a foot control so the clinician can adjust the chair without using their hands. Upholstery is typically seamless and wipe-clean, with disposable barrier covers on high-touch areas between patients. When buying a chair on its own, check compatibility with existing delivery units, lights and suction, along with patient weight capacity and footprint.

dental-extraction-instruments.description: Dental extraction instruments are the hand instruments used to loosen and remove teeth, combining elevators and luxators with extraction forceps. Straight, Cryer and other elevators are wedged between tooth and bone to stretch ligament fibres and lift the tooth or root, while luxators have thinner, sharper blades for gentler, bone-preserving work; forceps then grasp and deliver the tooth. Instruments come in tooth-specific and left/right paired patterns. Clinics usually assemble procedure trays for common extraction types, and blade tips should be inspected for damage after each reprocessing cycle.

dental-forceps.description: Dental forceps are hinged extraction instruments with beaks shaped to grip specific teeth, used to luxate and remove teeth in dental clinics and oral surgery. Upper forceps have straight or bayonet-style handles aligned with the maxillary arch, while lower forceps have beaks set roughly at right angles to the handles for the mandible. Patterns are tooth-specific, for example incisors and canines, premolars, molars with beaks that engage the root furcation, and root fragments. Clinics typically stock sets covering adult and child teeth, and hinge action and beak alignment should be checked regularly.

dental-mirrors.description: Dental mirrors are handheld instruments with a small round mirror head used to view hard-to-see tooth surfaces, reflect light into the mouth and retract the cheek or tongue during examination and treatment. Common head sizes are No. 4 and No. 5, about 22 mm and 24 mm, on screw-in or cone-socket fittings that attach to compatible handles. Front-surface mirrors give a sharper single image than rear-surface designs. Heads are cleaned and sterilised between patients and replaced when scratched or cloudy, since a worn surface reduces visibility.

dental-probes.description: Dental probes are fine-tipped instruments used to examine teeth and gums. Periodontal probes have a blunt, millimetre-marked tip for measuring pocket depth and attachment loss during periodontal charting, while explorers have a sharp point for detecting calculus, restoration margins and surface irregularities. Designs include colour-banded and ball-ended periodontal probes and double-ended explorer and probe combinations. Stainless steel probes are reprocessed and sterilised between patients, disposable plastic versions are available for single use, and markings must stay clearly legible for accurate charting.

dental-scalers.description: Dental scalers remove calculus, plaque and stains from tooth surfaces during routine cleaning and periodontal treatment. Hand scalers, such as sickle scalers for deposits above the gumline, have sharp working edges that need regular sharpening, while related curettes have rounded tips for work below the gumline. Ultrasonic and other powered scalers vibrate a fine tip at high frequency with a water spray to break up deposits and flush the area. Powered units need compatible tips or inserts and a water supply, and high-volume suction is recommended to control aerosols.

dental-suction-systems.description: Dental suction systems remove saliva, water, blood and aerosols from the mouth during treatment, keeping the field clear and reducing airborne contamination. A central vacuum unit connects to high-volume evacuator tubes and low-volume saliva ejectors at each chair, with disposable tips changed between patients. In dry systems fluid is separated near the chair, while wet systems carry fluid and air together to the vacuum unit. Size the system for the number of chairs used at the same time, and plan for amalgam separation where required and regular cleaning of suction lines.

dental-units.description: Dental units are integrated treatment centres combining a patient chair, instrument delivery unit, operating light, assistant's module and often a cuspidor in one system. The delivery unit holds handpiece hoses, an air/water syringe and sometimes an ultrasonic scaler or curing light, while the assistant's side carries high- and low-volume suction. Delivery can be mounted over the patient, at the side or behind the chair, which affects four-handed working. Key selection factors include waterline disinfection, the number of instrument positions, compatibility with existing compressors and suction plant, and team ergonomics.

dental-x-ray-machines.description: Dental X-ray machines are small radiography units used to take intraoral images such as bitewing and periapical views for diagnosing caries, periodontal bone loss and root problems. Wall-mounted units use an articulating arm to position the tube head at the patient's mouth, while handheld or portable units allow imaging in small clinics and outreach settings. They are used with digital sensors, phosphor plates or film. Rectangular collimation and fast image receptors help reduce patient dose, and installation must account for operator distance and shielding requirements.

diagnostic-sets.description: Diagnostic sets combine an otoscope head and an ophthalmoscope head on a shared battery handle, packed in a carry case so clinicians can examine ears, eyes and often the nose and throat with one kit. They are used in outpatient clinics, on ward rounds, in community visits and in teaching, where portability and quick switching between examinations matter. Sets typically include reusable and disposable ear specula, spare bulbs and sometimes a nasal speculum or throat illuminator. When choosing, check the bulb type, the handle's power source and whether heads and handles can be replaced individually.
diagnostic-sets.specifications: Components: otoscope head, ophthalmoscope head, battery handle; Accessories: ear specula, spare bulbs, optional nasal speculum; Illumination: halogen, xenon or LED; Power: dry-cell or rechargeable handle; Storage: hard or soft carry case

digital-bp-monitors.description: Digital BP monitors are automatic devices that inflate the cuff, sense pressure oscillations in the artery and display systolic and diastolic pressure and pulse rate on a screen, with no stethoscope needed. Upper-arm models are preferred in clinical settings, while wrist models are more compact; many store readings, average several measurements and flag irregular heartbeats. They suit outpatient triage, ward rounds and home monitoring programmes. Accuracy depends on the correct cuff size, keeping the arm at heart level and a rested patient, and oscillometric readings can be unreliable in some arrhythmias.
digital-bp-monitors.specifications: Method: oscillometric; Cuff pressure range: approx. 0–299 mmHg; Pulse range: approx. 40–180 bpm; Memory: stored readings, multi-user on some models; Cuffs: adult, large adult, paediatric; Power: batteries and/or AC adapter

digital-thermometers.description: Digital thermometers are electronic contact thermometers that use a sensor in the probe tip to measure body temperature and show the result on a small display, usually within several seconds to about a minute. They are used for oral, axillary and rectal readings in wards, clinics and emergency departments, and some models offer a faster predictive mode and memory of the last reading. Disposable probe covers are commonly used to prevent cross-contamination between patients. Normal values differ by measurement site, so record which site was used, and keep separate, clearly marked thermometers for rectal use.

digital-x-ray-systems.description: Digital X-ray systems are fixed, room-based radiography installations that capture images on a digital flat-panel detector instead of film, displaying them within seconds for review. A typical room includes a high-frequency generator, an X-ray tube on a ceiling or floor mount, a patient table and a wall stand for chest and upright studies. Digital capture removes chemical processing, allows image adjustment after exposure and supports sending images to PACS. Planning considerations include room shielding, power supply, detector size and whether one or two detectors are needed for table and wall-stand workflow.

disinfectant-sprayers.description: Disinfectant sprayers are reusable devices that apply disinfectant solutions to surfaces, equipment and rooms in an even, controlled spray. Handheld trigger and pump-pressure sprayers of 0.5 to 5 litres suit spot treatment of bed areas, trolleys and benches, while larger battery-powered electrostatic units cover wider areas with charged droplets that wrap around surfaces. Bottles and seals must be chemically compatible with the product used, such as chlorine, alcohol or quaternary ammonium disinfectants. Surfaces must stay wet for the disinfectant's stated contact time, and in many settings spraying onto a cloth is preferred to reduce aerosol exposure.
disinfectant-sprayers.specifications: Type: trigger, pump-pressure or electrostatic; Capacity: 0.5–5 L handheld, larger units available; Nozzle: adjustable mist to jet; Materials: chemical-resistant HDPE/PP with resistant seals; Power: manual or rechargeable battery

disposable-bedpans.description: Disposable bedpans are single-use bedpans for patients who cannot get out of bed to use the toilet. Most are made of moulded pulp, hold about 2 to 2.5 litres, and are placed in a reusable plastic support for strength while in use. After use the pulp pan goes into a macerator, which removes the need to wash and disinfect steel or plastic bedpans and lowers the risk of cross-infection. Confirm that the pulp products are compatible with the ward's macerator and with the supports already in stock.
disposable-bedpans.specifications: Material: moulded pulp; Capacity: about 2–2.5L; Support: reusable plastic holder; Disposal: macerator; Use: single use, non-sterile

disposable-bowls.description: Disposable bowls are single-use containers for holding water, saline, antiseptic or other solutions during bedside care, wound cleaning, procedures and patient washing. Capacities of 500mL to 1000mL cover tasks from soaking swabs to bed baths. They are moulded from plastic or pulp fibre, with sterile versions for aseptic procedures and non-sterile versions for general care. Single use removes the washing and reprocessing needed for steel bowls. Pulp bowls can often go into a macerator, while plastic bowls hold liquids for longer without softening.
disposable-bowls.specifications: Capacity: 500–1000mL; Material: polypropylene or moulded pulp; Sterility: non-sterile, sterile options; Disposal: pulp versions often macerator compatible; Use: single use

disposable-cups.description: Disposable cups in clinical settings include small graduated medicine cups and larger drinking cups. Medicine cups of about 30mL are marked in millilitres for measuring and giving oral liquid medicines and for holding tablets on medication rounds. Drinking cups of about 200–250mL are used for patient hydration, mouth rinsing and general laboratory use. Single use reduces cross-contamination compared with washing and reusing cups. Check that graduations are clearly printed or moulded, and that the material suits hot liquids where needed.
disposable-cups.specifications: Medicine cups: about 30mL, graduated in mL; Drinking cups: about 200–250mL; Material: polypropylene, polystyrene or paper; Packaging: sleeves or bulk cartons; Use: single use, non-sterile

disposable-isolation-gowns.description: Disposable isolation gowns are non-sterile, single-use gowns worn over clothing to protect the arms and torso of staff from contact with blood, body fluids and other potentially infectious material during patient care. They are used in isolation rooms, emergency departments and general wards, and are made from polypropylene nonwoven, SMS or film-laminated fabrics with elastic or knitted cuffs and neck and waist ties. They come in universal or free size and XL. Choose the fabric for the expected exposure: lightweight nonwoven for dry contact precautions, and fluid-resistant laminated or coated gowns when splashes are likely.
disposable-isolation-gowns.specifications: Material: PP nonwoven, SMS or PE-coated/laminated; Fabric weight: approx. 20–50 gsm; Cuffs: elastic or knitted; Closure: neck and waist ties, open back; Length: below knee; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use

disposable-kidney-dishes.description: Disposable kidney dishes are curved, kidney-shaped receivers that fit against the patient's body to catch vomit or sputum, and to hold used instruments, swabs and dressings during procedures. Sizes run from small, around 250mL, to large, around 750mL. They are moulded from pulp fibre or plastic; pulp versions can often be disposed of in a macerator, avoiding the washing of reusable steel dishes. Sterile versions are available for aseptic procedures. Choose larger, deeper dishes for emesis and smaller sizes for instruments and swabs.
disposable-kidney-dishes.specifications: Sizes: small about 250mL to large about 750mL; Material: moulded pulp or plastic; Sterility: non-sterile, sterile options; Disposal: pulp versions often macerator compatible; Use: single use

disposable-pe-gloves.description: Disposable PE gloves are thin, loose-fitting gloves cut and heat-sealed from polyethylene film. They give a basic barrier for brief, low-risk tasks such as handling food trays, changing linen, dispensing supplies, applying creams or touching clean surfaces in wards and home care. Because the film is not elastic and the seams are welded rather than moulded, they do not fit closely and puncture easily, so they are not a substitute for examination gloves when contact with blood, body fluids or sharp instruments is expected. They are typically sold in one size or S to L, often in bulk packs or tear-off pads.

disposable-syringes.description: Disposable syringes are sterile, single-use plastic syringes used to draw up and inject medicines, flush lines and collect samples. They range from 1mL for small doses to 50–60mL for feeds, irrigation and syringe pumps. Tips may be luer slip, where the needle pushes on, or luer lock, which screws on securely and is preferred for pumps and pressurised injections; larger syringes are also made with catheter tips. Most have a clear polypropylene barrel and rubber plunger seal. Choose the smallest syringe that holds the dose for easier reading of graduations.
disposable-syringes.specifications: Sizes: 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50–60mL; Tip: luer slip, luer lock, or catheter tip on large sizes; Barrel: clear polypropylene with printed graduations; Needle: with or without attached needle; Packaging: individually sterile-packed

disposable-underpads.description: Disposable underpads are absorbent pads placed on beds, trolleys, chairs and examination couches to protect surfaces and linen from urine, wound drainage and other fluids. A typical pad has a soft non-woven top sheet, a fluff pulp core, sometimes with superabsorbent polymer, and a waterproof plastic backing. Common sizes are 60x60cm for chairs and procedures and 60x90cm for beds. They are also used under patients during procedures and on laboratory benches. Choose absorbency by need, and avoid layering several pads on pressure-relieving mattresses.
disposable-underpads.specifications: Sizes: 60x60cm, 60x90cm; Top layer: non-woven; Core: fluff pulp, with or without superabsorbent polymer; Backing: waterproof polyethylene film; Use: single use, non-sterile

disposable-urinals.description: Disposable urinals are single-use urine bottles for bed-bound or less mobile patients. Male urinals, usually about 1000mL to 1500mL, have an angled neck, while female urinals have a wider, shaped opening to fit the body. Most are moulded pulp for macerator disposal, sometimes used with a reusable support, and some versions carry volume graduations for measuring output. Single use reduces cross-infection and cleaning workload compared with reusable bottles. Check whether graduations are needed for fluid balance monitoring before choosing a style.
disposable-urinals.specifications: Types: male and female; Capacity: male about 1000–1500mL; Material: moulded pulp or plastic; Disposal: pulp versions macerator compatible; Use: single use, non-sterile

dressing-sets.description: Dressing sets are sterile, single-use procedure packs containing the basic items needed to change a dressing or clean a wound from one opening. A standard pack includes plastic forceps, a gallipot for cleansing solution, gauze swabs and a sterile drape or field, with some versions adding gloves or a waste bag. Using a pre-assembled set saves preparation time, reduces handling of loose supplies and supports aseptic non-touch technique at the bedside. Check contents against local procedure needs, since forceps type and swab count vary between packs.

dressing-trolleys.description: Dressing trolleys are mobile stainless-steel carts used to carry and lay out supplies for wound dressing, catheterisation and other bedside procedures. A typical trolley has two or three shelves, a smooth top surface for setting up a sterile field, and a side holder for a waste bag, with some adding drawers or bowl rings. Swivel casters, often with brakes, let it move easily between beds. The top shelf should be cleaned and disinfected before each procedure, and smooth welded corners make this quicker and more thorough.

dry-heat-sterilizers.description: Dry heat sterilizers sterilize items with hot air rather than steam, typically at around 160–180°C, with longer exposure times needed at the lower temperatures. They suit materials that steam would damage or cannot penetrate, such as laboratory glassware, metal instruments prone to corrosion or dulling, powders, oils and petroleum-based products. Benchtop units with forced-air circulation heat more evenly and run shorter cycles than static gravity-convection ovens. Because the high temperatures can damage plastics, rubber and some instrument coatings, check item compatibility first, and allow loads to cool fully before handling.

duodenoscopes.description: Duodenoscopes are side-viewing flexible endoscopes used mainly for endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), giving a direct view of the major papilla in the duodenum. Their distinctive feature is an elevator at the tip that deflects cannulas, guidewires, sphincterotomes and stents into the bile or pancreatic duct. Typical insertion-tube diameters are around 11–12 mm, with large working channels for therapeutic accessories. Because the elevator area is complex to clean, these scopes need meticulous manual cleaning and strict adherence to reprocessing instructions; designs with disposable distal caps can simplify this.
duodenoscopes.specifications: View: side-viewing; Insertion tube: approx. 11–12 mm; Working channel: approx. 3.7–4.2 mm; Elevator: accessory elevator at distal tip; Working length: approx. 1240 mm; Reprocessing: high-level disinfection or sterilisation

ecg-monitors.description: ECG monitors continuously display and record the heart's electrical activity through skin electrodes, letting staff watch heart rate and rhythm and detect arrhythmias as they happen. Three-lead and five-lead configurations are used for ongoing rhythm monitoring in ICUs, wards, emergency departments and during transport, while 12-lead capability gives a fuller view for assessing ischaemia. Common features include heart-rate and arrhythmia alarms, ST-segment analysis on some models, trend storage and printing. Electrode placement and skin preparation strongly affect signal quality, so stock compatible disposable electrodes and lead sets for the patient sizes you treat.
ecg-monitors.specifications: Lead configurations: 3-, 5- or 12-lead; Display: colour screen with multiple waveform traces; Functions: heart-rate and arrhythmia alarms, ST analysis on some models; Recording: thermal printer or digital export on many models; Power: mains with battery backup

elastic-bandages.description: Elastic bandages are stretchable woven bandages containing elastic yarns that give support and moderate compression for sprains, strains and soft-tissue injuries, and hold dressings or splints in place. Widths run from 5cm for wrists and hands up to 15cm for thighs and the trunk, and they are fastened with clips or hook-and-loop closures. Most are washable and reusable, with single-use versions for infection control. Apply with even overlap and steady tension, and check fingers or toes for colour and sensation to avoid restricting circulation.

electric-hospital-beds.description: Electric hospital beds use motor-driven actuators to adjust height, backrest, knee section and often tilt at the push of a handset or nurse control panel. Powered height adjustment lets staff raise the bed to a safe working height for care and lower it to reduce fall risk, while profiling helps with breathing, feeding and pressure redistribution. Common features include split side rails, central braking, battery backup and a CPR quick-release. Weight capacity typically ranges from 135kg to 185kg. Confirm mattress platform size and whether patient lockout controls are included.

electric-wheelchairs.description: Electric wheelchairs are battery-powered chairs driven by motors and steered with a joystick, allowing users with limited arm strength or endurance to move independently at home, in the community and around wards. Designs range from lightweight folding travel chairs to heavier models with longer range, suspension and tilt or recline seating for complex needs, in standard and bariatric widths. Rechargeable batteries determine driving range and need routine charging. Assessment should consider the user's ability to operate the controls safely, the terrain and doorways involved, transport needs and access to servicing.

electrical-stimulation-units.description: Electrical stimulation units are multi-channel therapy devices used by physiotherapists for muscle strengthening and re-education, pain relief and oedema management. Going beyond basic TENS, they typically offer waveforms such as neuromuscular stimulation (NMES), interferential, Russian and high-voltage pulsed current, with programmable on/off cycles, ramp times and intensity on each channel. Clinic models may be combined with ultrasound therapy or vacuum electrodes, while portable versions support home exercise programmes. Choose according to the waveforms your service uses, the number of channels needed to treat several muscle groups at once and electrode consumable costs.
electrical-stimulation-units.specifications: Channels: 2–4 or more; Waveforms: TENS, NMES, interferential, Russian, high-voltage; Controls: intensity, frequency, ramp, on/off time; Programmes: preset and user-defined; Electrodes: self-adhesive, carbon or sponge

electrosurgical-pencils.description: Electrosurgical pencils are hand-held instruments that connect to an electrosurgical generator and deliver monopolar current through an interchangeable electrode tip. Hand-switched pencils have rocker or push buttons to select cut and coagulation, while foot-controlled versions rely on a separate footswitch. Most are supplied sterile for single use with an attached cable and standard blade electrode, and reusable handle variants also exist. Extended-length tips reach deep cavities, and coated tips reduce charred tissue build-up. Confirm the connector matches the generator before ordering.
electrosurgical-pencils.specifications: Activation: hand-switch (rocker or push button) or footswitch; Electrode: blade standard, needle or ball optional; Tip length: standard and extended; Cable: integrated with generator connector; Supply: sterile, single use (reusable handles available)

electrosurgical-plates.description: Electrosurgical plates, also called patient return electrodes or grounding pads, are adhesive pads that collect monopolar current from the patient and route it safely back to the generator. Applied to clean, dry skin over a well-perfused muscle mass near the surgical site, they spread the current over a large area to prevent burns where it exits. Split-pad designs work with return-electrode monitoring to alarm when contact becomes poor. Adult and paediatric sizes are available; the adhesive surface is single-use, and pads should never be cut or repositioned.
electrosurgical-plates.specifications: Type: solid or split (dual-section) pad; Sizes: adult and paediatric; Contact surface: conductive adhesive gel; Cable: pre-attached or separate reusable cable; Use: single use

electrosurgical-units.description: Electrosurgical units are generators that deliver high-frequency electrical current to cut tissue and coagulate bleeding vessels during surgery. Most general-purpose hospital units offer both monopolar output, used with a handpiece and a patient return electrode, and bipolar output, used with forceps that pass current only between their tips. Cut, blend and coagulation modes are selected on the front panel, with power adjustable up to around 300W. When choosing a unit, check return-electrode monitoring, alarm functions and compatibility with the pencils, forceps and pads already in use.
electrosurgical-units.specifications: Output modes: monopolar cut, blend and coagulation, plus bipolar; Power: adjustable, typically up to about 300W; Safety: return-electrode monitoring and alarms; Activation: handswitch and footswitch; Power supply: mains AC; Accessories: pencils, bipolar forceps, return pads

emergency-carts.description: Emergency carts, or crash carts, are lockable multi-drawer trolleys that keep resuscitation drugs, airway equipment, IV supplies and a defibrillator together for cardiac arrest and other emergencies. The top surface typically holds the defibrillator or monitor, with a CPR board on the back and an IV pole and oxygen cylinder holder at the side. Drawers are often colour-coded or labelled by function, and numbered breakaway seals show whether stock has been opened. Standardise drawer layout across units so staff can find items quickly under pressure.
emergency-carts.specifications: Drawers: typically 4–6, lockable or seal-secured; Construction: steel, aluminium or ABS plastic; Accessories: IV pole, CPR board, oxygen holder, defibrillator shelf; Mobility: casters with brakes; Security: central lock or breakaway seals

emergency-stretchers.description: Emergency stretchers carry injured or ill patients from the scene, through ambulances and into the emergency department. Folding stretchers are lightweight and compact to store, scoop stretchers split lengthwise so they can be slid under a patient without log-rolling, and basket stretchers enclose the patient for rope, water or rough-terrain rescue. Frames are usually aluminium or plastic, with restraint straps and carrying handles, and typical capacity is 135kg to 180kg. Choose the type by rescue environment, storage space and whether the device should be X-ray translucent.
emergency-stretchers.specifications: Types: folding, scoop, basket; Frame: aluminium alloy or high-density polyethylene; Load capacity: typically 135–180kg; Restraints: patient straps included; Features: carrying handles, folds for storage

endoscope-cleaning-brushes.description: Endoscope cleaning brushes are used during manual cleaning of flexible endoscopes to remove organic debris from internal channels, valve ports and the distal tip before high-level disinfection. Channel brushes have bristles on a long flexible shaft pulled through the suction and working channels, while short or double-ended brushes clean valve cylinders and ports. Bristle diameter must match the channel: too small leaves debris behind, too large may not pass or may damage the lining. Single-use brushes avoid cleaning and inspecting brushes between uses, and sterile single-use variants are available where required.
endoscope-cleaning-brushes.specifications: Types: channel, valve-port and tip brushes; Bristle diameter: matched to channel size; Channel brush length: approx. 1500–2300 mm; Construction: nylon bristles on flexible shaft; Configuration: single- or double-ended

endoscopes.description: Flexible endoscopes are reusable instruments with a steerable insertion tube, light guide and video or fibre-optic imaging that let clinicians examine and treat the inside of the digestive tract. Gastrointestinal types include gastroscopes for the upper tract, colonoscopes for the large bowel and side-viewing duodenoscopes for biliary and pancreatic work, in adult and paediatric diameters. A working channel passes biopsy forceps, snares and other accessories, while air/water and suction channels keep the view clear. Confirm compatibility with the facility's video processor and light source, and a validated cleaning and high-level disinfection process, before purchase.
endoscopes.specifications: Types: gastroscope, colonoscope, duodenoscope; Imaging: video or fibre-optic; Tip deflection: four-way angulation; Channels: working, air/water and suction; Sizes: adult and paediatric diameters; Reprocessing: high-level disinfection

endoscopic-clips.description: Endoscopic clips (haemoclips) are small metal clips deployed through an endoscope's working channel to control bleeding, close mucosal defects and mark lesion sites. Each clip is preloaded on a flexible applicator: the operator opens the jaws, positions them over the target, then closes and releases the clip, which typically detaches on its own days to weeks later. Many designs can be rotated and reopened before final deployment for accurate placement. Standard and long-reach applicators suit upper GI and colonic use, and jaw opening width should match the defect or vessel size.
endoscopic-clips.specifications: Jaw opening: approx. 8–16 mm; Applicator: standard and long-reach lengths; Functions: rotatable, reopenable (design dependent); Min. channel: approx. 2.8 mm; Clip material: stainless steel or alloy

endoscopic-snares.description: Endoscopic snares are wire loops housed in a flexible plastic sheath that are passed through an endoscope channel to capture and remove polyps and other lesions. The loop is opened around the lesion and closed from the handle, cutting either cold or with electrosurgical current to cut and coagulate tissue. Loops come in hexagonal, oval and crescent shapes from about 10 mm to 30 mm, in braided or monofilament wire. Small cold snares are generally used for diminutive polyps and larger loops for bigger or pedunculated lesions; for hot snaring, confirm compatibility with the electrosurgical unit.
endoscopic-snares.specifications: Loop shape: hexagonal, oval, crescent; Loop diameter: approx. 10–30 mm; Wire: monofilament or braided stainless steel; Working length: approx. 2300 mm; Use: cold or hot (electrosurgical)

endotracheal-tubes.description: Endotracheal tubes are sterile, single-use tubes passed through the mouth or nose into the trachea to secure the airway, allow mechanical ventilation and protect the lungs from aspiration. They are usually clear PVC with a radiopaque line, depth markings and a Murphy eye, and come cuffed, with a high-volume low-pressure cuff and pilot balloon, or uncuffed. Sizes run from 2.5 mm internal diameter for neonates to about 9.0 mm for large adults, with variants such as reinforced, preformed oral or nasal, and subglottic suction tubes. Cuff pressure should be checked regularly to avoid leaks or tracheal injury.
endotracheal-tubes.specifications: Material: PVC with radiopaque line; Sizes: ID 2.5–9.0 mm, usually in 0.5 mm steps; Cuff: cuffed (high-volume low-pressure) or uncuffed; Features: Murphy eye, depth markings, 15 mm connector; Variants: reinforced, preformed, subglottic suction; Sterility: sterile, single-use

examination-lamps.description: Examination lamps provide focused, adjustable light for physical examinations and minor procedures such as wound inspection, suturing, and gynaecological and ENT examinations. They come as mobile floor-stand models on castors, wall-mounted units and table-top versions, usually with a flexible gooseneck or articulated arm to position the beam. Most current lamps use LEDs, which give bright, cool light with little heat at the patient and a long service life. When selecting for a room, consider light intensity, spot size, colour rendering, the reach of the arm and how easily the head can be cleaned.
examination-lamps.specifications: Light source: LED (halogen on older models); Colour temperature: approx. 4,000–5,000 K; Mounting: mobile stand, wall or table-top; Arm: gooseneck or articulated; Controls: on/off, dimming on many models

exercise-bikes.description: Rehabilitation exercise bikes are stationary cycles used to build cardiovascular fitness, lower-limb strength and joint range of motion in physiotherapy, cardiac and post-operative rehabilitation. Recumbent and seated designs with a backrest and step-through frame are easier and safer to mount for older or deconditioned patients than upright bikes. Resistance is adjustable, often magnetically, and displays show time, speed, distance and sometimes heart rate, while some models start at very low resistance or add arm cranks for upper-body work. Check seat adjustment range, maximum user weight and footprint for the space available.
exercise-bikes.specifications: Type: recumbent or seated upright; Resistance: magnetic or friction, adjustable levels; Display: time, speed, distance, heart rate; Access: step-through frame; Seat: adjustable position with backrest

face-shields.description: Face shields are clear visors that cover the eyes, nose, mouth and sides of the face, protecting healthcare workers from splashes and sprays of blood, body fluids and chemicals. They consist of a transparent PET, polycarbonate or acetate visor held by a foam headband and elastic strap, or by a reusable frame or glasses-style holder that takes replaceable visors. They can be worn over surgical masks, respirators and prescription glasses. Anti-fog coating and a visor that extends below the chin matter most for comfort and coverage; a face shield does not replace respiratory protection.
face-shields.specifications: Visor material: PET, polycarbonate or acetate; Visor thickness: approx. 0.2–0.5 mm; Coating: anti-fog; Headgear: foam band with elastic strap, or reusable frame; Size: one size, adjustable; Sterility: non-sterile

feeding-pumps.description: Enteral feeding pumps deliver liquid nutrition through a nasogastric, nasojejunal or gastrostomy tube at a controlled rate when patients cannot eat enough by mouth. They are used in ICU and wards for continuous or intermittent feeding, typically at 1 to 300 mL/h, and many can also schedule water flushes. Dedicated enteral sets with non-luer connectors help prevent feed being connected to an IV line by mistake. Alarms cover occlusion, empty bag and low battery. Check set compatibility, portability for mobile patients and ease of cleaning.
feeding-pumps.specifications: Rate: typically 1–300 mL/h; Modes: continuous, intermittent, water flush; Sets: dedicated enteral sets with enteral-only connectors; Alarms: occlusion, feed empty, low battery; Power: mains and rechargeable battery; Mounting: IV pole clamp

fetal-dopplers.description: Fetal Dopplers are handheld ultrasound devices that detect the fetal heartbeat and show fetal heart rate, used at antenatal visits and for intermittent auscultation in labour. A main unit with loudspeaker and digital display connects to a probe at around 2–3 MHz: 2 MHz gives deeper penetration for later pregnancy or larger patients, while 3 MHz offers good sensitivity earlier in gestation. Coupling gel is needed for signal transmission, and some units offer waterproof probes. Staff should confirm the detected rate is fetal rather than maternal by checking the mother's pulse at the same time.
fetal-dopplers.specifications: Probe frequency: 2–3 MHz; Display: digital FHR readout with audio speaker; Form: handheld, single or interchangeable probe; Power: rechargeable or disposable batteries; Accessories: coupling gel, optional waterproof probe

fetal-monitors.description: Fetal monitors, also called cardiotocographs, record fetal heart rate and uterine contractions to assess fetal well-being during pregnancy and labour. An ultrasound transducer detects the fetal heartbeat and a pressure (toco) transducer tracks contractions, both held on the abdomen with elastic belts and coupling gel, and many models add fetal movement marking and a printed or digital trace. Single and twin monitoring versions are available for antenatal clinics and labour wards. Reliable traces need correct transducer positioning and periodic confirmation that the recorded heart rate is fetal rather than maternal.
fetal-monitors.specifications: Parameters: FHR (ultrasound), uterine activity (toco), fetal movement; Channels: single or twin FHR; Recording: thermal printer and/or digital storage; Options: maternal heart rate, SpO2 or NIBP on some models; Accessories: transducer belts, coupling gel

foam-dressings.description: Foam dressings are absorbent polyurethane pads used on moderately to heavily exuding wounds such as pressure injuries, leg ulcers, skin tears and donor sites. The foam takes up fluid while keeping a moist wound environment, and cushions the area against pressure and friction. Bordered versions with adhesive or silicone edges stay in place without tape, while non-bordered foam needs a secondary fixation and suits fragile skin. Sizes range from about 5x5cm to 20x20cm, with shaped heel and sacral versions. They are less suited to dry wounds.

gastroscopes.description: Gastroscopes are forward-viewing flexible endoscopes designed for upper GI endoscopy, examining the oesophagus, stomach and duodenum. A typical adult instrument has an insertion tube of about 9 mm and a working length of around 1000 mm, with a channel of roughly 2.8 mm for biopsy forceps, injection needles and other accessories. Slim and ultra-slim versions are available for paediatric or transnasal use, while therapeutic models have larger channels for haemostasis and foreign body removal. Tip angulation, channel size and compatibility with the existing video processor are key selection points.
gastroscopes.specifications: Insertion tube: approx. 9 mm (slim approx. 5–6 mm); Working length: approx. 1000–1100 mm; Working channel: approx. 2.8 mm (therapeutic 3.2 mm+); View: forward-viewing; Angulation: four-way tip deflection; Reprocessing: high-level disinfection

gauze.description: Gauze is a loosely woven cotton fabric used to clean wounds, absorb blood and exudate, pack cavities, pad and cover dressings, and apply solutions. It is supplied as folded pads, commonly 5x5cm, 7.5x7.5cm and 10x10cm, and as rolls for bandaging or cutting to size. Sterile packs are used on open wounds and during procedures, while non-sterile bulk rolls suit general cleaning and padding. Gauze can stick to a drying wound bed and shed fibres, so a non-adherent dressing may be preferable directly on fragile wounds.

gauze-swabs.description: Gauze swabs are pre-cut, folded squares of woven cotton gauze used for wound cleaning, applying antiseptics, absorbing blood during procedures and as a secondary dressing layer. They are graded by size, typically 5x5cm, 7.5x7.5cm and 10x10cm, and by ply from about 4 to 16 layers, with higher ply giving more absorbency and padding. Swabs intended for surgery may include an X-ray detectable thread so a retained swab can be located. Sterile packs suit open wounds, while non-sterile swabs serve general cleaning tasks.

gynecological-examination-tables.description: Gynaecological examination tables are couches designed for pelvic examination, speculum and colposcopy procedures and minor gynaecological work, supporting the patient in the lithotomy position. They feature padded leg supports or stirrups, an adjustable backrest and often a drainage tray, with height adjustment that brings the patient to a comfortable working level for the clinician. Manual, hydraulic and electric versions are available. Because a disposable paper roll is commonly used over the upholstery between patients, a built-in roll holder and wipe-clean, fluid-resistant covering help with hygiene and quick turnover.
gynecological-examination-tables.specifications: Adjustment: manual, hydraulic or electric; Height: adjustable working height; Leg supports: knee crutches or foot stirrups; Backrest: adjustable angle; Accessories: drainage tray, paper roll holder; Upholstery: wipe-clean, fluid-resistant

gynecological-instruments.description: Gynaecological instruments are reusable stainless steel tools for examination and minor procedures on the cervix and uterus, such as endometrial sampling, IUD insertion and dilation and curettage. Common items include tenaculums to grasp and steady the cervix, uterine sounds to measure uterine depth, graduated cervical dilators and sharp or blunt curettes, bought individually or as procedure sets. Instruments are cleaned and sterilised between patients, so corrosion-resistant surgical-grade steel and careful tracking of set contents help maintain availability and safe reprocessing.
