gynecological-instruments.specifications: Items: tenaculum, uterine sound, cervical dilators, curettes; Material: surgical stainless steel; Dilators: graduated sizes (e.g. Hegar type); Curettes: sharp or blunt, various sizes; Reprocessing: steam sterilisable

hand-sanitizers.description: Hand sanitizers are alcohol-based hand rubs used for hand hygiene at the point of care when hands are not visibly soiled, such as before and after patient contact and before aseptic tasks. Most contain ethanol or isopropanol, commonly 60–80 percent, with emollients to limit skin dryness, and come as gels, liquids or foams. Sizes range from 100 mL pocket bottles and pump bottles to 1–5 L refills for wall dispensers. Use enough to cover all hand surfaces and rub until dry, usually 20–30 seconds; soap and water is still needed for visibly soiled hands and some spore-forming organisms.
hand-sanitizers.specifications: Active: ethanol or isopropanol, approx. 60–80% v/v; Format: gel, liquid or foam; Additives: emollients; Pack sizes: 100 mL–5 L, pump bottles and refills; Dispensing: flip-top, pump or wall dispenser

heat-therapy-units.description: Heat therapy units, such as hydrocollators, are thermostatically controlled water tanks that keep hot packs at treatment temperature, ready for moist heat therapy in physiotherapy. Packs filled with silica gel or bentonite absorb heat and are wrapped in towelling covers before being placed on the neck, back, shoulders or limbs to relieve muscle spasm and stiffness. Tanks come in sizes holding a few to many packs, with standard, neck and oversize pack shapes. Choose tank capacity by patient throughput, and use enough insulating layers between pack and skin to prevent burns.
heat-therapy-units.specifications: Unit: stainless steel heated water tank; Temperature: thermostatic, approx. 70–75°C; Capacity: from a few to a dozen or more packs; Packs: silica gel or bentonite, various shapes; Accessories: towelling pack covers

hematology-analyzers.description: Hematology analyzers are automated laboratory instruments that perform a complete blood count from a small sample of anticoagulated whole blood, reporting red cells, white cells, platelets, haemoglobin, haematocrit and red cell indices. Three-part differential models sort white cells into lymphocytes, mid-sized cells and granulocytes by impedance, while five-part models add optical or flow-based methods to separate neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils and basophils. They rely on reagents, diluents and controls as ongoing consumables. Choose between 3-part and 5-part according to workload and clinical needs, and factor in reagent use, quality control and maintenance.
hematology-analyzers.specifications: Differential: 3-part or 5-part WBC; Sample: approx. 10–150 µL EDTA whole blood; Technology: impedance, plus optical/flow cytometry on 5-part; Throughput: approx. 30–100+ samples per hour; Data: QC software, LIS connectivity

hemoglobin-analyzers.description: Hemoglobin analyzers are compact point-of-care devices that measure haemoglobin concentration from a single drop of capillary or venous blood, drawn into a disposable microcuvette or applied to a test strip and read photometrically, usually within about a minute. They are used for anaemia screening in outpatient and antenatal clinics, blood donor selection and wards where a quick result helps before full laboratory testing. Many are battery-operated and portable for outreach work. Good capillary sampling technique matters, as squeezing the finger hard or using the first drop can dilute the sample with tissue fluid and give falsely low results.
hemoglobin-analyzers.specifications: Method: photometric or reflectance; Sample: approx. 10 µL capillary or venous blood; Measuring range: approx. 0–25 g/dL; Test time: under about 60 s; Consumables: microcuvettes or strips, sterile lancets; Power: battery or mains

hemostatic-forceps.description: Hemostatic forceps, often called artery forceps or haemostats, are locking surgical instruments used to clamp blood vessels and control bleeding during open procedures. A ratchet lock between the finger rings holds the jaws closed so the surgeon's hands are free, and serrated jaws grip tissue without slipping. Common patterns include the fine-tipped Mosquito, the mid-sized Kelly and the longer Rochester-Pean, in straight or curved forms from about 12.5cm to 20cm. Choose length and jaw delicacy to suit vessel size and wound depth, and inspect ratchets and jaw alignment after each reprocessing cycle.

high-flow-oxygen-systems.description: High-flow oxygen systems deliver heated, humidified air-oxygen mixtures at up to 60 L/min through wide-bore nasal cannulas, with oxygen concentration set independently of flow. The high flow matches or exceeds the patient's own inspiratory demand, flushes carbon dioxide from the upper airway and adds a small positive pressure, while warmth and humidity improve comfort and help clear secretions. They are used for acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure, after extubation and in emergency and ward settings. Cannula prongs should fill no more than about half of each nostril so that gas can escape around them.
high-flow-oxygen-systems.specifications: Flow range: up to approx. 60 L/min adult, lower paediatric ranges; FiO2: approx. 21–100%, adjustable; Humidification: heated, approx. 31–37°C; Interface: wide-bore nasal cannula or tracheostomy adapter; Consumables: heated circuit, humidifier chamber

home-nebulizers.description: Home nebulizers are compact devices that turn liquid medication into a fine aerosol for inhalation, allowing patients with asthma, COPD and other lung conditions to take treatments at home. Compressor models are mains-powered tabletop units that are durable and simple to use, while handheld vibrating mesh devices are quieter, battery-powered and easy to carry when travelling. Kits usually include a medication cup, tubing, mouthpiece and adult or child masks, which are replaced periodically. The medication cup should be cleaned and dried after each use, and the device should suit the prescribed medication.

home-oxygen-concentrators.description: Home oxygen concentrators draw in room air and use molecular sieve beds to remove nitrogen, delivering concentrated oxygen through a nasal cannula or mask for long-term oxygen therapy at home. Stationary units run on mains power and commonly provide continuous flow up to about 5 L/min, while portable battery models often use pulse-dose delivery to save oxygen when the patient is mobile. Concentrators reduce reliance on frequent cylinder deliveries. Patients should use the prescribed flow rate, keep the unit ventilated and away from open flames, and have a backup cylinder in case of power failure.

hospital-beds.description: Hospital beds are adjustable beds built for patient care in wards, outpatient areas and clinics, positioning the patient for comfort, treatment and safer handling by staff. Models range from simple fixed-height or crank-operated beds to two- and three-function electric beds, typically with backrest and knee sections, side rails, removable head and foot boards and lockable casters. Weight capacity is usually 135kg to 185kg on standard-width platforms. When choosing, weigh budget against the positions needed, staff handling demands and the reliability of power supply.

hydrocolloid-dressings.description: Hydrocolloid dressings contain gel-forming agents such as carboxymethylcellulose on a waterproof film or foam backing. In contact with wound fluid they form a soft gel that keeps the wound moist, supports autolytic debridement and keeps out water and bacteria. They suit light to moderately exuding wounds, superficial pressure injuries and minor burns, and thin versions protect at-risk skin. Sizes range from about 5x5cm to 20x20cm. They are not suited to heavily exuding or infected wounds, and a gel with mild odour on removal is normal.

hypodermic-needles.description: Hypodermic needles are sterile single-use needles that attach to a syringe through a luer hub for injections, drawing up medicines and aspirating fluid. Gauge sets the bore: 18G and 19G suit drawing up and viscous fluids, 21G to 23G suit intramuscular injections and venepuncture, and 25G to 27G suit intradermal and subcutaneous injections. Lengths range from about 13mm to 38mm, and hubs are colour-coded by gauge for quick identification. Select length according to injection route and patient size, and keep a sharps container at the point of use.
hypodermic-needles.specifications: Gauges: 18G–27G; Lengths: about 13–38mm (1/2 to 1 1/2 inch); Hub: colour-coded by gauge, luer compatible; Bevel: regular or short; Packaging: individually sterile-packed

icu-beds.description: ICU beds are fully powered critical care beds for patients who need frequent repositioning, close monitoring and rapid intervention. Beyond standard electric profiling, they typically add Trendelenburg and reverse Trendelenburg, a quick CPR function that flattens the platform, an integrated weighing scale, angle indicators and nurse controls built into the side rails. Radiolucent backrests on many models allow chest X-rays without moving the patient. Weight capacity is commonly 180kg to 250kg. Check compatibility with pressure-relieving mattresses and the battery backup duration.

icu-patient-monitors.description: ICU patient monitors continuously display and record vital signs for critically ill patients and alarm when values cross set limits. Beyond standard ECG, SpO2, non-invasive blood pressure, respiration and temperature, ICU models commonly add invasive pressure channels for arterial and central venous lines, capnography and cardiac output measurement, often through plug-in modules. Large touchscreens show waveforms and trends, and units can network to a central station for remote viewing. Check the number of parameter slots, arrhythmia analysis features and compatibility with existing central systems.
icu-patient-monitors.specifications: Standard parameters: ECG, SpO2, NIBP, respiration, temperature; Optional: invasive pressure, EtCO2, cardiac output; Display: colour touchscreen, waveform and trends; Connectivity: central station networking; Alarms: configurable audible and visual; Power: mains with battery backup

immobilization-devices.description: Immobilization devices hold an injured patient's head, spine and body in position during extrication, transport and imaging. Head blocks attach to a spine board or stretcher to stop the head turning, vacuum mattresses mould around the body and become rigid when air is drawn out, and vest-type extrication devices stabilise the head and torso of a seated patient trapped in a vehicle. Most are made of washable, radiolucent materials and fastened with colour-coded straps. Choose devices that fit existing boards and stretchers, and check vacuum mattresses for leaks.
immobilization-devices.specifications: Types: head immobilisers, vacuum mattresses, extrication vests; Material: closed-cell foam and coated fabric; Fastening: hook-and-loop and buckle straps; Features: radiolucent, wipe-clean; Accessories: hand or foot pump for vacuum mattresses

infant-incubators.description: Infant incubators are enclosed, transparent chambers that provide a warm, humidified and protected environment for preterm, low-birth-weight or sick newborns. Unlike open radiant warmers, they maintain a stable microclimate using servo control of air or skin temperature and adjustable humidity, which helps reduce heat and fluid loss in very small infants. Hand ports and access doors allow care with minimal disturbance, and many units offer a tilting mattress tray, integrated scale or oxygen inlet. Alarm functions, ease of cleaning between patients and whether a transport model is also needed are key considerations.

infant-warmers.description: Infant radiant warmers are open-bed units that supply overhead radiant heat to keep newborns warm while leaving the baby fully accessible for resuscitation, assessment and procedures. A heater head above a height-adjustable bassinet tray works in manual mode or servo mode, where a skin temperature probe adjusts heat output automatically. Many units include an Apgar timer, tilting tray, X-ray cassette drawer and alarms for probe disconnection or overheating. Because the open design increases insensible water loss, radiant warmers are generally preferred for short-term care in delivery rooms and during procedures.

infrared-lamps.description: Infrared lamps provide superficial heat therapy by emitting infrared radiation onto the skin, used in physiotherapy to relax muscles, ease stiffness and reduce pain before exercise or manual therapy. Floor-standing models on castors and compact table-top units are available, with adjustable height and head angle to direct heat onto the treatment area. A protective guard over the bulb and a treatment timer support safe use. Lamps should be set at the recommended distance from the skin, and clinicians should check skin sensation beforehand and monitor the patient during treatment to avoid burns.
infrared-lamps.specifications: Type: floor-standing or table-top; Adjustment: height and head angle; Heat source: infrared bulb or emitter; Controls: on/off with treatment timer; Safety: protective guard; Power: mains

infrared-thermometers.description: Infrared thermometers measure body temperature by detecting infrared energy emitted from the skin or eardrum, giving a reading in about a second. Forehead and temporal models work without contact or by scanning across the forehead, which helps with screening and with sleeping or uncooperative patients, while tympanic models read inside the ear canal, usually with a disposable probe cover. They are used in triage, wards, outpatient clinics and paediatric areas. Results can be affected by sweat, room temperature, earwax and technique, so let the device adjust to the room and follow the stated measuring distance and positioning.

infusion-pumps.description: Volumetric infusion pumps deliver IV fluids, medicines and blood products at a programmed rate and volume through an administration set. They are used when a gravity drip is not accurate enough, such as for continuous drug infusions, fluid balance in the ICU or timed infusions on wards. Rates typically range from 0.1 to 999 mL/h, with alarms for air-in-line, occlusion, door open and infusion complete, and many models include drug libraries with dose limits. Confirm which administration sets the pump accepts, since dedicated sets add ongoing consumable cost.

instrument-disinfectants.description: Instrument disinfectants are chemical solutions used to disinfect reusable medical devices that cannot be heat sterilized, or to decontaminate instruments before further processing. High-level disinfectants such as glutaraldehyde, ortho-phthalaldehyde and peracetic acid are used for semi-critical devices like endoscopes and ultrasound probes, while lower-level detergent-disinfectant formulations suit general instruments and pre-soaking. They are supplied as concentrates for dilution or ready-to-use solutions in 1 to 5 litre containers. Instruments must be thoroughly cleaned first, fully immersed for the stated contact time and rinsed afterwards, and reusable solutions need regular concentration testing.
instrument-disinfectants.specifications: Actives: glutaraldehyde, OPA, peracetic acid, hydrogen peroxide or QAC-based; Level: high-level or intermediate/low-level; Format: concentrate or ready-to-use; Pack sizes: 1–5 L; Reuse: single-use or reusable for a stated period with test strips

instrument-tables.description: Instrument tables, often called back tables, are larger stainless-steel worktops used to set out the full range of sterile instruments, drapes and supplies for a procedure. Unlike a Mayo stand, which holds only the instruments in immediate use over the patient, the back table stays beside the scrub team and carries the complete set. Designs range from simple flat tables to models with a lower shelf, raised edges or drawers, all on casters. Choose a size that suits the room layout and the procedures performed.
instrument-tables.specifications: Material: stainless steel; Top: flat, with or without raised rim; Configuration: single top or top with lower shelf; Mobility: casters, some lockable; Use: covered with sterile back-table drape

instrument-trays.description: Instrument trays are reusable stainless steel trays and baskets used to organise, hold and transport surgical instruments through cleaning, inspection, packing and sterilization. Perforated or wire mesh baskets let water, detergent and steam circulate and drain, while solid trays are used for laying out instruments or as procedure trays. Many sets use silicone mats, pins or brackets to keep delicate instruments separated and protected. They come in small to large sizes, with or without lids and handles. Choose a size that holds the set in a single layer, as overloading hampers cleaning, steam penetration and drying.
instrument-trays.specifications: Material: stainless steel (304 or 316 grade); Style: perforated, wire mesh or solid, with or without lid; Sizes: small to large, often sized to fit standard containers; Accessories: silicone mats, instrument pins, handles; Compatibility: washer-disinfector and steam sterilization

insulin-syringes.description: Insulin syringes are small-volume syringes with a fine 30G or 31G needle permanently attached for subcutaneous insulin injection. Barrels are graduated in insulin units rather than millilitres: the 0.3mL size holds up to 30 units, 0.5mL up to 50 units and 1mL up to 100 units of U-100 insulin. The fixed needle leaves very little dead space, so little insulin is wasted. Choose the smallest barrel that fits the dose for easier, more accurate reading, and make sure the syringe calibration matches the insulin concentration in use.
insulin-syringes.specifications: Capacities: 0.3mL (30 units), 0.5mL (50 units), 1mL (100 units); Calibration: U-100 insulin; Needle: fixed, 30–31G, short length; Dead space: low; Packaging: sterile, single use

intermittent-catheters.description: Intermittent catheters are designed for repeated, regular bladder emptying, often by patients or caregivers performing clean intermittent self-catheterisation at home. Hydrophilic-coated versions become slippery when wetted and pre-lubricated gel versions reduce friction, while uncoated catheters need separate lubricant. Compact and ready-to-use designs, some with an integrated collection bag, make catheterisation easier away from a toilet. Sizes run from 6Fr to 20Fr, with shorter female and longer male lengths. Each catheter is sterile and single use; user dexterity and comfort guide the choice.

irrigation-tubes.description: Endoscopic irrigation tubes are single-use tubing sets that deliver sterile water through an endoscope's auxiliary water-jet channel or working channel to wash away blood, stool, bile or mucus and keep the visual field clear. They typically run from a water bottle or bag via an irrigation pump or flushing syringe and include a connector matched to the scope's channel port, often with a backflow-prevention valve. Sets come in different lengths and diameters for gastroscopes and colonoscopes. Confirm connector compatibility with the scope and pump in use, and replace sets as directed to limit cross-contamination.
irrigation-tubes.specifications: Use: water-jet or working-channel irrigation; Connection: scope-specific or luer connector; Valve: one-way backflow prevention; Length: various to suit pump or bottle position; Fluid: sterile water

iv-administration-sets.description: IV administration sets connect a fluid bag or bottle to a patient's cannula or catheter for gravity infusion or use with a pump. Each set includes a spike, a drip chamber, tubing, a roller clamp for rate control, an injection port and a luer connector. Standard macro-drip sets deliver about 20 drops per mL for routine fluids, while micro-drip sets deliver about 60 drops per mL for precise low-volume or paediatric infusions. Some include an air vent for rigid bottles or an in-line filter. Always confirm the drop factor before calculating drip rates.
iv-administration-sets.specifications: Drop factor: about 20 drops/mL standard, about 60 drops/mL micro-drip; Components: spike, drip chamber, roller clamp, injection port, luer connector; Options: air vent, in-line filter; Material: medical-grade PVC or DEHP-free; Packaging: sterile, single use

iv-extension-sets.description: IV extension sets add length or extra access points between an IV catheter and the main administration line. Extra length lets patients move without pulling on the cannula, and short extensions keep line changes away from the insertion site, reducing manipulation of the catheter hub. Sets come in various lengths with single or multiple lumens, with or without injection ports, slide or pinch clamps and needle-free connectors. Small-bore versions keep dead volume low for syringe pump use. Match connector type and priming volume to the infusion.
iv-extension-sets.specifications: Lengths: short to long, various; Configurations: single, dual or triple lumen; Ports: with or without injection site or needle-free connector; Clamps: slide or pinch; Connectors: luer lock; Packaging: sterile, single use

iv-fluids.description: IV fluids are sterile solutions given directly into a vein to replace fluid and electrolytes, maintain hydration and act as a carrier for diluted medicines. Common types include 0.9% sodium chloride, lactated Ringer's, dextrose solutions in water or saline, and other balanced electrolyte solutions. They come in flexible bags or bottles from about 50mL, used for drug dilution, up to 1000mL for fluid replacement. The choice of solution and volume is a prescribing decision; for supply, check container type, port design and compatibility with administration sets.
iv-fluids.specifications: Common solutions: 0.9% sodium chloride, lactated Ringer's, dextrose 5% and 10%, dextrose-saline; Volumes: 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000mL; Container: PVC or non-PVC bag, or bottle; Ports: administration port and injection port; Storage: room temperature, protect from freezing

iv-preparation-equipment.description: IV preparation equipment provides a controlled clean environment for aseptic compounding of intravenous medicines, parenteral nutrition and cytotoxic drugs in hospital pharmacies. Main types are laminar airflow cabinets, which pass HEPA-filtered air over the work area, biological safety cabinets that also protect the operator when handling hazardous drugs, and enclosed isolators with glove ports. Sterile disposable consumables such as syringes and transfer sets are used inside the controlled zone. Aseptic technique remains essential, so choose equipment according to the drugs prepared, the room classification and cleaning and validation requirements.
iv-preparation-equipment.specifications: Types: laminar airflow cabinet, biological safety cabinet, isolator; Filtration: HEPA-filtered air; Airflow: horizontal or vertical unidirectional; Work surface: stainless steel; Monitoring: airflow alarm or indicator

kn95-respirators.description: KN95 respirators are disposable filtering facepiece respirators made to a performance class requiring at least 95 percent filtration of airborne particles, comparable in filtration to N95 respirators. Most use a folding, multi-layer design with ear loops and a nose clip in a single adult size, which makes them convenient but generally less consistent at achieving a tight face seal than head-strap respirators. They are used for general respiratory protection in clinics, wards and support areas. Where a fit-tested respirator is required, such as during aerosol-generating procedures, confirm the model can pass a fit test before relying on it.

laryngeal-masks.description: Laryngeal masks are supraglottic airway devices with an inflatable cuff that sits over the laryngeal inlet, attached to an airway tube that exits through the mouth, providing a clear airway without entering the trachea. They are widely used for shorter anaesthetic procedures and as a rescue airway when face-mask ventilation or intubation is difficult. Sizes run from 1 for neonates to 5 for large adults, chosen mainly by body weight. Most are sterile single-use PVC devices, while reusable silicone versions can be reprocessed a limited number of times. Classic designs do not reliably protect against aspiration, so patient selection matters.

latex-surgical-gloves.description: Latex surgical gloves are sterile, single-use gloves made from natural rubber latex and shaped to the hand, with curved fingers and a long cuff that sits over the gown sleeve. Latex offers high elasticity, a close fit and fine tactile sensitivity, which is why it remains common for procedures that need precise instrument handling. They are sized in half sizes from 5.5 to 8.5 and supplied as individually packed pairs. Natural rubber proteins can trigger allergic reactions, so check for latex allergy in both the surgical team and the patient before use, and keep a latex-free alternative available.

leg-bags.description: Leg bags are body-worn urine collection bags that strap to the thigh or calf and connect to an indwelling urethral or suprapubic catheter, letting ambulant patients move around discreetly during the day. They typically hold 350 mL to 750 mL and include an inlet tube, a non-return valve to limit backflow and a lever or twist-tap outlet for emptying, with elastic straps or a fabric sleeve holding the bag in place. Choose capacity and inlet-tube length to suit the wearer's mobility and preferred bag position, and link to a larger night drainage bag for overnight use.
leg-bags.specifications: Capacity: 350–750 mL; Inlet tube: short, long or cut-to-length; Valve: non-return anti-reflux valve; Outlet: lever, push or twist tap; Fixing: elastic straps or leg sleeve; Fluid path: sterile, single use

mammography-systems.description: Mammography systems are dedicated X-ray units that image breast tissue at low dose for breast cancer screening and diagnostic assessment. A compression paddle flattens and holds the breast against a digital detector to reduce motion and tissue overlap, while a low-kilovoltage tube with molybdenum, rhodium or tungsten target optimises soft-tissue contrast. Many digital systems also offer tomosynthesis (3D imaging) and support stereotactic biopsy. Planning should cover room shielding, review workstation requirements, an ongoing quality control programme and whether screening volumes justify tomosynthesis capability.
mammography-systems.specifications: Detector: digital flat panel, approx. 24 × 30 cm; Tube voltage: low kVp, typically approx. 25–35; Anode: molybdenum, rhodium or tungsten; Compression: motorised with manual release; Options: tomosynthesis, stereotactic biopsy

manual-hospital-beds.description: Manual hospital beds are adjusted with hand cranks at the foot end rather than motors, usually with two or three cranks controlling backrest, knee break and sometimes height. With no electrical parts they are simpler to maintain, need no power supply and suit general wards, step-down areas and sites with unreliable electricity. Typical features include side rails, removable head and foot boards, an IV pole socket and lockable casters. Weight capacity generally runs from 135kg to 150kg. Choose the number of cranks according to the positions patients need.

manual-wheelchairs.description: Manual wheelchairs are self-propelled or attendant-pushed chairs for people who cannot walk or can walk only short distances, used at home, in the community and for hospital transport. Self-propelled models have large rear wheels with push rims, while transit models have small wheels and are pushed by a carer. Folding steel or aluminium frames suit storage and car transport, and narrow, standard and bariatric widths cover weight capacities of roughly 100–200 kg. Seat width and depth should fit the user to reduce pressure injury and poor posture, and swing-away footrests and removable armrests ease transfers.

mayo-stands.description: A Mayo stand is a small, height-adjustable instrument tray on a single upright that slides over the patient so the instruments in immediate use are within reach of the scrub nurse and surgeon. A U-shaped or offset base on casters lets it roll in close to the operating table without hitting the table base. The removable stainless-steel tray is covered with a sterile Mayo stand cover before instruments are laid out. Check the height range against the operating table and how easily the height lock can be adjusted.
mayo-stands.specifications: Material: stainless steel frame and tray; Height: adjustable with knob or foot-operated lock; Base: U-shaped or offset on casters; Tray: removable flat tray; Use: with sterile Mayo stand cover

medical-refrigerators.description: Medical refrigerators are purpose-built cold storage units that hold temperature-sensitive medicines, reagents and laboratory samples within a tight 2–8°C range, avoiding the fluctuations of domestic fridges. They use forced-air circulation for even temperature, a digital controller and display, and audible and visual alarms for high or low temperature and door-open events. Capacities typically run from about 100 L to 700 L in under-counter and upright formats, with solid or glass doors and lockable access. Data logging or remote monitoring helps document temperature control, and siting away from heat sources supports stable performance.

medical-tape.description: Medical tape secures dressings, IV cannulas, tubing and catheters to the skin. Main types include breathable paper tape for fragile skin and frequent changes, transparent plastic tape that resists water and tears easily, silk-like cloth tape with strong hold, zinc oxide tape for heavy-duty fixation and strapping, and silicone tape that removes gently. Widths of 1.25cm, 2.5cm and 5cm on 5–9 metre rolls are common. Match adhesive strength to the patient's skin condition and the device being secured, and remove tape slowly, low and close to the skin.
medical-tape.specifications: Types: paper, transparent plastic, silk-like cloth, zinc oxide, silicone; Widths: 1.25cm, 2.5cm, 5cm; Roll length: 5–9m; Adhesive: acrylic, zinc oxide or silicone; Options: hypoallergenic and latex-free

medical-waste-treatment-systems.description: Medical waste treatment systems decontaminate infectious waste on site or at a central facility so it can be disposed of as non-hazardous waste. Autoclave-based systems use pressurised steam, often combined with shredding to reduce volume and make waste unrecognisable, while chemical systems combine disinfectants with mechanical maceration. Throughput ranges from compact units for a single facility to larger systems serving several sites. Selection depends on daily waste volume and type, space and utilities, operator training and the validation testing needed to show effective treatment; pharmaceutical and some chemical waste need other disposal routes.

medical-waste-trolleys.description: Medical waste trolleys are wheeled carts used to move bagged clinical waste safely from wards and departments to the central holding area. They are usually made of rigid plastic or metal with closed bodies and lids that contain bags and prevent spills, and lockable lids restrict access during transport and storage. Sizes range from small ward carts to large wheeled bins. Smooth, wipe-clean surfaces and drain points help with disinfection, and dedicated trolleys colour-coded for each waste stream keep waste separated all the way to disposal.

medication-cabinets.description: Medication cabinets are lockable cupboards that keep medicines in pharmacies, ward medication rooms and clinics organised, secure and away from unauthorised access. They are usually powder-coated or stainless steel with adjustable shelves, bins or drawers, in wall-mounted and floor-standing formats, including double-locked cabinets for controlled drugs and glass-fronted designs for visibility. Clear labelling and bin dividers support stock rotation and reduce picking errors. Select the lock type and security level according to the class of medicines stored and local controlled-drug storage rules.
medication-cabinets.specifications: Material: powder-coated or stainless steel; Mounting: wall-mounted or floor-standing; Interior: adjustable shelves, bins or drawers; Locking: key, combination or electronic; Options: double-lock controlled-drug compartment, glass doors

medication-trolleys.description: Medication trolleys are mobile, lockable carts used to carry and give medicines during ward rounds, keeping patients' medicines organised and secure at the bedside. They usually have multiple drawers or cassette bins, a work surface and key, code or electronic locking, with optional controlled-drug compartments, waste bins and holders for charts or a computer. Some designs use individual patient drawers for unit-dose systems. Choose a drawer layout that matches the ward's dispensing system, and check castor quality, manoeuvrability and how quickly the trolley can be locked when left unattended.
medication-trolleys.specifications: Body: steel, aluminium or ABS plastic; Drawers: multi-drawer or patient-specific cassettes; Locking: key, combination or electronic; Castors: swivel with brakes; Options: controlled-drug box, side bins, laptop shelf

microscope-slides.description: Microscope slides are flat glass plates, standardly 25mm by 75mm and about 1mm thick, on which specimens are mounted for examination under a microscope. Plain slides suit general work, frosted-end slides can be labelled in pencil, and charged or coated slides help tissue sections and cytology specimens adhere during staining. Ground or cut edges and pre-cleaned surfaces are common, and slides are used with cover slips. Most are discarded after use, especially with infectious material. Frosted or colour-coded ends help accurate specimen identification.

microscopes.description: Laboratory microscopes are compound light microscopes used to examine blood smears, urine sediment, stained tissue, microbiology preparations and other specimens. Binocular heads suit routine work, while trinocular heads add a port for a camera to capture and share images. Typical objectives run from 4x to 100x oil immersion, combined with 10x eyepieces, a mechanical stage, an Abbe condenser and LED illumination. Plan achromat objectives give a flatter field across the image. Consider phase contrast or fluorescence options for specialised work, and protect optics from humidity and fungus.

mobile-x-ray-systems.description: Mobile X-ray systems are trolley-mounted radiography units pushed or motor-driven to the bedside for patients who cannot be moved, commonly used for chest and bedside films in wards, ICU, theatres and emergency departments. They carry a generator, articulating tube arm and often an integrated digital detector and display, so images can be reviewed at the bedside. Motor-assisted drive and a compact footprint make it easier to manoeuvre between beds. Consider generator power, battery capacity for full rounds, detector integration and tube-arm reach when choosing a system.

monopolar-electrosurgical-units.description: Monopolar electrosurgical units send current from an active electrode, such as a pencil blade or needle tip, through the patient's body to a dispersive return pad placed on the skin. This makes them suited to cutting and coagulating over larger areas in general, orthopaedic and plastic surgery. Typical modes include pure cut, blended cut and several coagulation settings, with power adjustable from about 1W to 300W. Because current crosses the body, correct return-pad placement and caution around implanted devices are essential, and return-electrode quality monitoring helps reduce burn risk.
monopolar-electrosurgical-units.specifications: Modes: pure cut, blend, coagulation (including spray/fulguration); Power range: about 1–300W; Return electrode: required, often with contact-quality monitoring; Activation: hand or foot switch; Electrodes: blade, needle and ball tips

n95-respirators.description: N95 respirators are tight-fitting, disposable filtering facepiece respirators designed to filter at least 95 percent of airborne particles, protecting the wearer against aerosols such as those carrying tuberculosis or measles. They come in cup, flat-fold and duckbill shapes with head straps and a malleable nose clip, and some include an exhalation valve. Protection depends on an airtight seal, so users should be fit-tested to a specific model and size, here S, M or L, and perform a seal check every time they put one on. Surgical versions add fluid resistance for use during procedures.

nasal-cannulas.description: Nasal cannulas are lightweight tubes with two short prongs that sit just inside the nostrils to deliver low-flow supplemental oxygen while leaving the mouth free for eating, drinking and talking. The tubing loops over the ears and adjusts under the chin, and soft, curved prongs aid comfort during long-term use. They are disposable and made in adult, paediatric and neonatal sizes for wards, ICUs, emergency departments and home oxygen. Standard cannulas are generally run at about 1 to 6 L/min in adults; higher flows dry the nasal lining, so humidification or a high-flow system is used when more oxygen is needed.

nebulizers.description: Nebulizers convert liquid medication into a fine mist inhaled through a mask or mouthpiece, delivering bronchodilators, steroids, antibiotics or saline directly to the airways. Compressor or jet nebulizers are robust and economical but noisier, vibrating-mesh units are quiet, portable and leave less medication behind, and ultrasonic models are quiet but not suitable for every drug. They are used in emergency departments, wards, clinics and at home, especially for children and patients who struggle with inhalers. Medication cups, masks and tubing should be cleaned and dried after each use or replaced to prevent contamination.

needle-destroyers.description: Needle destroyers render used hypodermic needles unusable immediately after an injection, reducing needlestick injuries and preventing reuse. Electric benchtop units melt or burn the needle using an electric arc or resistive heating, while manual or mechanical units cut the needle from the syringe hub into a sealed collection container, with residues then disposed of as sharps waste. Consider which needle sizes the unit accepts, power or battery availability and the residue container capacity. Units are most useful at the point of use, such as injection rooms and vaccination stations.
needle-destroyers.specifications: Type: electric (arc or resistive heating) or manual cutter; Compatibility: standard hypodermic needles; Power: mains or rechargeable battery (electric types); Collection: sealed residue container; Placement: benchtop

needle-holders.description: Needle holders, also called needle drivers, are locking instruments that grip a curved suture needle firmly while the surgeon passes it through tissue. Compared with hemostats they have shorter, heavier jaws, often with a cross-hatched or tungsten carbide insert that stops the needle rotating. Patterns range from the general-purpose Mayo-Hegar to finer Webster or Crile-Wood holders, in lengths of roughly 12cm to 20cm. Match jaw size to needle size, since a fine needle clamped in a heavy jaw can bend or flatten, and check the jaw surface for wear during reprocessing.

nelaton-catheters.description: Nelaton catheters are straight, single-lumen urinary catheters with a rounded closed tip and side drainage eyes, used for short-term bladder drainage, in-and-out catheterisation and collecting sterile urine samples. Unlike Foley catheters they have no retention balloon, so they are removed once the bladder is empty. Usually made of PVC, they come in sizes from 6Fr to 20Fr with colour-coded connectors, in male, female and paediatric lengths. Choose the smallest size that drains effectively, and insert with sterile lubricant and aseptic technique.

neonatal-monitors.description: Neonatal monitors are multi-parameter patient monitors configured for newborns, tracking heart rate, respiration, SpO2, temperature and non-invasive blood pressure in the NICU and nursery. They use neonatal-specific sensors, including small ECG electrodes, wrap-style oximetry probes and neonatal cuffs, with alarm limits set for newborn ranges and apnoea detection. Some support transcutaneous gas monitoring, invasive pressures or central station networking. Alongside screen visibility and alarm management, consider the ongoing supply and cost of disposable neonatal sensors, which are usually single-patient use.

neonatal-ventilators.description: Neonatal ventilators provide mechanical breathing support for newborns with respiratory failure, prematurity-related lung disease or apnoea, delivering very small, precisely controlled breaths. They can deliver tidal volumes as low as about 2 mL and typically use a flow sensor at the airway to measure volumes and compensate for the endotracheal tube leaks common in infants. Modes may include pressure-controlled, volume-targeted and CPAP, and some units offer high-frequency ventilation. The ventilator is reusable while breathing circuits are typically disposable, so confirm the circuits, humidifier and sensor consumables available for the chosen model.

nitrile-surgical-gloves.description: Nitrile surgical gloves are sterile, single-use gloves made from synthetic nitrile rubber and are a common latex-free choice for operating theatres and procedure rooms. Nitrile contains no natural rubber proteins, so it suits staff and patients with latex allergy, and it generally offers good puncture and chemical resistance. The gloves are anatomically shaped, sized 5.5 to 8.5 in half sizes and packed as sterile pairs. Nitrile is usually somewhat less elastic than latex, so trying adjacent sizes or a softer formulation helps surgeons find a snug fit without hand fatigue during long cases.

non-woven-swabs.description: Non-woven swabs are made from bonded synthetic or blended fibres, such as viscose and polyester, rather than woven cotton threads. They are softer, shed fewer fibres and are less likely to stick to wounds than woven gauze while remaining absorbent, which makes them useful for wound cleaning, skin preparation, applying solutions and general dressing care. Common sizes are 5x5cm, 7.5x7.5cm and 10x10cm, usually in 4-ply. Sterile and non-sterile packs are available, and higher-ply swabs suit wounds with heavier exudate.
non-woven-swabs.specifications: Material: viscose/polyester non-woven; Sizes: 5x5cm, 7.5x7.5cm, 10x10cm; Ply: typically 4-ply; Weight: commonly 30–40 gsm; Sterility: sterile packs or non-sterile bulk

operating-room-stools.description: Operating room stools provide seating for surgeons, anaesthetists and scrub staff during long or seated procedures such as ophthalmic, ENT, dental and hand surgery. They typically have a stainless-steel or coated steel frame, a padded seat with wipe-clean upholstery and a five-caster base. Height is adjusted by gas lift or a rotating screw mechanism, and models come with or without a backrest, some adding a foot ring. Look for smooth-rolling casters and seamless upholstery that is easy to disinfect between cases.
operating-room-stools.specifications: Frame: stainless steel or coated steel; Height adjustment: gas lift or screw; Seat: padded, wipe-clean upholstery; Backrest: optional; Base: five casters, some with foot ring

operating-tables.description: Operating tables support and position the patient during surgery, letting the team raise, tilt and articulate the tabletop for access to the operative site. Tops are divided into head, back, seat and leg sections, and usually provide Trendelenburg, reverse Trendelenburg, lateral tilt and flex movements. Tables may be mechanical-hydraulic, electro-hydraulic or fully electric, and specialty versions suit orthopaedic, urology or general surgery, with weight capacity typically from 135kg to 450kg. Check for radiolucent sections if intraoperative imaging is needed, and confirm accessory rail compatibility.
operating-tables.specifications: Drive: manual hydraulic, electro-hydraulic or electric; Movements: height, Trendelenburg, lateral tilt, back and leg sections; Load capacity: typically 135–450kg, bariatric higher; Tabletop: radiolucent options; Accessories: side rails, arm boards, head and leg rests

ophthalmoscopes.description: Direct ophthalmoscopes are handheld instruments that let clinicians look through the pupil at the retina, optic disc and blood vessels, and examine the lens and front structures of the eye. They are used in outpatient clinics, wards and emergency departments when assessing conditions such as diabetic and hypertensive retinopathy, papilloedema and cataract. A rotating lens wheel corrects for the refractive error of patient and examiner, and interchangeable apertures and filters, such as small spot, slit, grid and red-free, suit different pupil sizes and findings. Examination is easier in a darkened room, with dilated pupils when appropriate.
ophthalmoscopes.specifications: Type: direct, handheld; Lens wheel: wide diopter range, commonly about -20 to +20 D or more; Apertures: small/large spot, slit, grid, red-free filter; Illumination: halogen or LED; Power: rechargeable or dry-cell battery handle

orthopedic-surgical-gloves.description: Orthopedic surgical gloves are sterile, single-use surgical gloves made in a heavier gauge than standard surgical gloves to withstand the demands of bone and joint surgery. The thicker wall gives more resistance to tears and punctures from bone fragments, wires, saws and sharp-edged implants, and many have a textured surface for a firm grip on wet instruments. They are commonly sized 6.5 to 9.0. The added thickness reduces tactile sensitivity, so some surgical teams pair them with a thinner inner glove in a double-gloving system rather than relying on gauge alone.

otoscopes.description: Otoscopes are handheld instruments for examining the ear canal and eardrum, combining a light source, a magnifying lens and a cone-shaped speculum inserted into the ear. They are used in outpatient clinics, wards and emergency departments to assess ear infections, wax impaction, foreign bodies and eardrum perforation. Fibre-optic models carry light through the head for a bright, shadow-free view, and pneumatic versions let the examiner puff air to test eardrum mobility. Use the largest speculum that fits comfortably, with disposable specula to prevent cross-infection, and keep spare bulbs or batteries on hand.
otoscopes.specifications: Illumination: halogen, xenon or LED, direct or fibre-optic; Magnification: approx. 3x, swing-away lens on many models; Specula: reusable or disposable, approx. 2–5 mm tips; Power: battery handle or wall-mounted transformer; Options: pneumatic insufflation port

oxygen-concentrators.description: Oxygen concentrators draw in room air and pass it through molecular sieve beds that remove nitrogen, delivering oxygen-enriched gas continuously without the need for cylinders. They are used for long-term oxygen therapy at home, in wards and clinics, and as a supplementary supply where piped oxygen is limited. Stationary units typically provide continuous flow from about 1 to 10 L/min, while portable models often use pulse-dose delivery. Purity generally falls as flow increases, so match the rated flow to the prescription, and plan for a reliable power supply, filter cleaning, space around the unit and a backup cylinder.

oxygen-flowmeters.description: Oxygen flowmeters control and display the rate of oxygen delivered to a patient, connecting to a wall outlet on a piped gas system or to a regulated cylinder. Thorpe-tube models have a clear tube with a floating ball read against a scale, while dial or click-style models offer preset flow steps. A range of 0–15 L/min is common, with low-flow versions for neonates and paediatrics. They are often fitted with a humidifier bottle when supplying masks and cannulas. Thorpe tubes must be mounted upright to read correctly, and the inlet probe must match the facility's wall-outlet type.
oxygen-flowmeters.specifications: Type: Thorpe tube (float) or click/dial; Range: 0–15 L/min standard, low-flow ranges available; Inlet: wall-outlet probe or threaded, matched to system; Outlet: barbed nipple or humidifier connection; Body: polycarbonate tube with metal housing

oxygen-masks.description: Oxygen masks deliver supplemental oxygen through a soft, clear mask covering the nose and mouth, connected by tubing to an oxygen source. Simple masks give moderate concentrations at medium flows, venturi masks use colour-coded adapters to deliver a set and more precise oxygen percentage, and non-rebreather masks with a reservoir bag and one-way valves provide high concentrations in emergencies. They are disposable, single-patient devices in adult and paediatric sizes. Run each type within its recommended flow range: simple masks need enough flow to flush out exhaled carbon dioxide, and a non-rebreather's reservoir bag should stay inflated.

oxygen-regulators.description: Oxygen regulators attach to an oxygen cylinder valve and reduce the high cylinder pressure to a safe, steady low pressure for patient delivery. Most combine a contents gauge showing cylinder pressure with a click-style flow selector or flowmeter, and connect through a pin-index yoke or a threaded fitting depending on the valve type. They are used with portable cylinders for patient transport, emergency trolleys, ambulances and home care. Choose a regulator that matches the cylinder valve and required flow range, open the cylinder valve slowly, and keep the regulator free of oil and grease, which can ignite in high-pressure oxygen.
oxygen-regulators.specifications: Inlet: pin-index yoke or threaded, matched to cylinder valve; Inlet rating: typical medical cylinder pressures (approx. 150–200+ bar); Flow: click-style approx. 0–15 L/min or flowmeter outlet; Gauge: cylinder contents gauge; Body: brass or aluminium

parallel-bars.description: Parallel bars are a pair of fixed handrails used in physiotherapy for gait training, standing balance and early mobilisation, letting patients practise walking with secure handholds on both sides. Rails are height-adjustable and often width-adjustable to fit children and adults, mounted on a stable floor-standing base or platform. Some models include an abduction board, a mirror at the end of the walkway or a non-slip platform. Choose a length that suits the available space and training goals, and check adjustment locks and base stability regularly, since patients may bear considerable weight through the rails.
parallel-bars.specifications: Length: approx. 2–4 m; Height: adjustable, child to adult; Width: adjustable between rails; Rails: wood or steel; Base: floor-standing platform or fixed uprights; Options: abduction board, gait mirror

patient-gowns.description: Patient gowns are loose-fitting garments worn by patients during admission, examinations, imaging and procedures, giving staff easy access to the body while preserving modesty. Traditional designs open at the back and fasten with ties or snaps, and some add shoulder snaps or side openings for IV lines and monitoring leads. Reusable versions are usually cotton or polyester-cotton fabric that withstands repeated laundering, while disposable nonwoven variants suit isolation or short outpatient stays. Sizes include S to XL plus adult and paediatric cuts; a generous back overlap improves coverage and patient comfort.
patient-gowns.specifications: Material: cotton or poly-cotton (reusable), PP/SMS nonwoven (disposable); Closure: back ties or snaps; Sleeves: short or sleeveless, shoulder snaps on some; Length: approx. knee length; Sterility: non-sterile

patient-monitors.description: Patient monitors are bedside devices that continuously measure and display vital signs, commonly ECG, heart rate, SpO2, non-invasive blood pressure, temperature and respiration, with waveforms, trends and alarms. They are used in ICUs, wards, operating and recovery rooms and emergency departments, and range from compact transport units to modular monitors that accept extra parameters such as invasive pressures or capnography. Battery backup keeps monitoring going during patient moves. When choosing, consider the parameters needed now and later, screen size, alarm management, adult, paediatric and neonatal settings, and whether the unit can network to a central station.
patient-monitors.specifications: Parameters: ECG, SpO2, NIBP, temperature, respiration; Options: IBP, EtCO2 on modular models; Display: colour screen, approx. 8–17 in; Patient types: adult, paediatric, neonatal; Power: mains with battery backup; Connectivity: wired or wireless link to central station

pediatric-beds.description: Pediatric beds and cots are hospital beds scaled for infants and children, from enclosed cots with high drop-sides to junior beds for older children. Tall side rails with narrow gaps reduce the risk of falls and entrapment, and many models offer backrest adjustment and tilt for clinical positioning. Frames are usually coated steel or stainless steel on lockable casters, often with colourful, wipe-clean panels. Select the size by the child's age and weight, and check that rail spacing and mattress fit match the manufacturer's specified patient population.

pediatric-bp-monitors.description: Pediatric BP monitors are blood pressure devices set up for neonates, infants and children, using smaller cuffs and, on automated models, inflation pressures and measurement settings adapted to small arms and faster heart rates. They are used in paediatric wards, NICUs and outpatient clinics, either as manual aneroid sets with a range of child cuffs or as automated oscillometric monitors with paediatric and neonatal modes. Cuff choice is critical: the bladder width should be about 40 percent of the arm circumference, as a cuff that is too large or too small gives falsely low or high readings. Select the patient mode matching the child's age and size.

pediatric-hospital-beds.description: Pediatric hospital beds are sized and designed for infants, children and adolescents, ranging from high-sided cots for toddlers to junior beds for older children. Full-length or high side rails help prevent falls, while adjustable height and backrest support nursing care, feeding and breathing comfort. Electric or manual models may also offer Trendelenburg positioning and a quick CPR release. Gaps between rails, mattress and frame must be small enough to prevent entrapment of small patients, and lockable castors, easy-clean surfaces and child-friendly finishes are practical points for busy paediatric wards.

pediatric-nebulizers.description: Pediatric nebulizers turn liquid medication into a fine mist for inhalation, delivering bronchodilators, steroids or saline to infants and children with asthma, bronchiolitis and other respiratory conditions. They are usually compressor (jet) or vibrating mesh devices supplied with child-sized face masks and mouthpieces, sometimes in playful designs that help young patients cooperate. Mesh units are quieter and more portable, while compressor models are robust and widely used on wards. A well-fitting mask is essential for children too young to use a mouthpiece, and medication cups and masks are typically disposable or single-patient items.

pediatric-pulse-oximeters.description: Pediatric pulse oximeters measure oxygen saturation (SpO2) and pulse rate non-invasively in infants and children by shining light through a finger, toe, hand or foot. They are used with paediatric-sized clip probes or soft wrap sensors that fit small digits and limbs, which matters because adult clips often give unreliable readings on children. Handheld and bedside units are common, often with motion-tolerant signal processing to cope with active or crying patients. Choose the probe by patient size and monitoring duration: clips suit spot checks, while wraps are better for continuous monitoring.

pediatric-scales.description: Pediatric scales weigh infants and children accurately so clinicians can track growth, monitor feeding and calculate weight-based medication doses. Infant scales have a curved tray that holds the baby securely and typically weigh up to about 20 kg in fine increments, while standing or seated scales are used for older children. Digital models often include tare, hold or averaging functions to give a stable reading on a moving baby. In the NICU and nursery, fine resolution and easy-clean trays are important, and some models add a length-measuring attachment for combined growth assessment.

pharmaceutical-waste-containers.description: Pharmaceutical waste containers are lidded, chemical-resistant containers for expired, unused or partly used medicines, including vials, tablets and contaminated packaging, keeping them apart from infectious and general waste. Sizes range from about 1 L for medication rooms to 20 L for pharmacies, usually with a secure closure that locks once full. Separate containers with distinct colour coding are often used for cytotoxic or other hazardous drugs. Correct segregation matters because pharmaceutical waste usually needs incineration or other specific treatment, so containers should be clearly labelled with the waste category.

pharmacy-refrigerators.description: Pharmacy refrigerators store refrigerated medicines such as insulin, some antibiotics, eye drops and biologics at 2–8°C in hospital pharmacies and ward medication rooms. They are designed around dispensing workflow, with adjustable shelves or drawers for stock rotation and segregation, glass doors so stock can be checked without opening, and locks to restrict access. Fan-assisted cooling, minimum/maximum temperature display and alarms help keep contents in range. Capacities usually span about 100 L to 600 L; choose a size that avoids overfilling, since tightly packed shelves block airflow and create warm spots.

phototherapy-units.description: Phototherapy units treat neonatal jaundice by exposing the infant's skin to blue light, which converts bilirubin into forms the body can excrete without relying on the liver to conjugate it. Overhead units sit above a cot, incubator or warmer, bili-blankets place a light-emitting pad around or under the baby, and bassinet-integrated designs build the light into the bed. Most current systems use blue LEDs. Effectiveness depends on irradiance and the skin area exposed, so units with adjustable, measurable irradiance are preferred, and eye shields are used with overhead lights.
phototherapy-units.specifications: Light source: blue LED (approx. 460–490 nm); Configuration: overhead, blanket/pad or bassinet; Irradiance: adjustable, standard and intensive levels; Controls: treatment timer; Accessories: eye shields, radiometer (optional)

pill-crushers.description: Pill crushers are handheld devices that grind tablets into powder so they can be mixed with soft food or liquid, or given through a feeding tube, for patients who cannot swallow tablets whole. Common designs use a screw-down, twist or lever action to crush tablets in a cup, and many work with disposable pouches or cups that contain the powder and reduce cross-contamination between patients; some also split tablets. Not every tablet is suitable for crushing, particularly modified-release, enteric-coated and some hazardous medicines, so pharmacy guidance should be checked first.
pill-crushers.specifications: Mechanism: screw-down, twist or lever; Operation: manual, handheld; Consumables: disposable crushing pouches or cups; Body: plastic or metal; Options: combined crusher and splitter

plasma-freezers.description: Plasma freezers store fresh frozen plasma, cryoprecipitate and other frozen blood components at about -18°C to -40°C. Some units also offer rapid freezing so plasma reaches its core storage temperature quickly after separation, helping preserve labile clotting factors. They come in upright or chest designs, typically 100L to 500L, with digital temperature control, data logging and alarms for temperature deviation and power failure. Frozen plasma bags are brittle, so look for drawers or racks that limit handling, and allow for compressor heat in the room.

plasma-sterilizers.description: Plasma sterilizers are low-temperature sterilizers that use vaporized hydrogen peroxide, energized into a plasma state, to sterilize heat- and moisture-sensitive devices such as endoscopic accessories, cameras, cables, batteries and some plastic instruments. Cycles run at low temperatures, generally below about 55°C, are relatively short, and leave mainly water vapour and oxygen as by-products, so loads need no aeration. Items must be clean and completely dry, and cellulose materials such as paper, linen and gauze cannot be processed, so compatible non-cellulose wraps and pouches are required. Lumen length and diameter limits vary by cycle and should be checked before loading.

plaster-bandages.description: Plaster bandages are rolls of gauze impregnated with plaster of Paris that harden after being dipped in water, used to make casts and back-slabs for fractures and post-operative immobilisation. They are easily moulded while wet for a close fit, set within minutes and reach full strength once dry. Widths of 5cm to 15cm suit fingers and wrists through to legs. Plaster is heavier and slower to dry than synthetic casting tape but is inexpensive and easy to shape. Pad the limb first, and use lukewarm water, since hot water speeds setting and raises heat.

portable-ultrasound-systems.description: Portable ultrasound systems are compact, battery-powered scanners in laptop-style or handheld formats, used for point-of-care imaging at the bedside and in emergency and outreach settings as well as imaging departments. They provide core B-mode and often colour Doppler imaging with one or a few interchangeable probes, and handheld types may use a tablet or smartphone as the display. Compared with cart-based systems they trade some image quality and features for mobility and fast start-up. Battery life, probe options, durability and how images are transferred to the patient record are key considerations.

portable-x-ray-machines.description: Portable X-ray machines are lightweight, compact units that can be carried or wheeled to the patient when moving them to radiology is impractical, such as on wards, in ICU and emergency departments and at outreach sites. Smaller than trolley-based mobile systems, they run on battery or mains power and are typically paired with a wireless digital detector or computed radiography cassettes. Their lower output compared with fixed rooms suits chest and extremity imaging. Operators must maintain radiation safety around nearby patients and staff, so consider exposure range, battery capacity, weight and stand options.

powder-free-surgical-gloves.description: Powder-free surgical gloves are sterile, single-use gloves made without donning powder, typically treated by chlorination or given an inner polymer coating that helps the glove slide on. Removing powder reduces the risk of powder-related wound inflammation and adhesions, lowers airborne latex proteins and avoids residue on implants and instruments. They are made in latex and in synthetic materials such as nitrile, polyisoprene or neoprene, in half sizes 5.5 to 8.5. When choosing, look at the base material as well as the coating, since together they determine allergy risk, grip and how easily the glove dons with damp hands.

powdered-examination-gloves.description: Powdered examination gloves are non-sterile, single-use gloves lightly dusted on the inside with an absorbable cornstarch powder so they slide on easily and stay comfortable when hands are damp. They are used for routine patient examinations, specimen handling and general nursing care in wards, outpatient clinics and laboratories, and are most often made from natural rubber latex or vinyl in sizes S to XL. Because the powder can carry latex proteins into the air and leave residue on wounds or lab samples, many facilities reserve them for low-risk tasks and choose powder-free gloves for wound care or latex-sensitive staff.

protective-aprons.description: Protective aprons are sleeveless coverings worn over uniforms to protect the front of the body from splashes, spills and soiling during tasks such as bathing patients, emptying drainage bags, handling soiled linen or cleaning instruments. Disposable aprons are thin polyethylene sheets, often supplied on rolls or in flat packs with a neck loop and waist ties, while reusable PVC or rubberized aprons are heavier and suit sluice rooms, CSSD and mortuary work. They are generally one size. Aprons leave the arms and back exposed, so a gown is preferred when arm contact or heavy contamination is expected.
protective-aprons.specifications: Material: PE film (disposable) or PVC/rubberized fabric (reusable); Width: approx. 70–80 cm; Length: approx. 105–125 cm; Fastening: neck loop and waist ties; Sterility: non-sterile

pulse-oximeters.description: Pulse oximeters estimate arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2) and pulse rate non-invasively by passing red and infrared light through a fingertip, earlobe or foot and measuring how much is absorbed. Fingertip models suit quick spot checks, while handheld and tabletop units with cable probes allow continuous monitoring, alarms and trend storage in wards, ICUs and emergency departments. Reusable clip and wrap probes come in adult, paediatric and neonatal sizes, and disposable covers or sensors reduce cross-contamination. Readings can be affected by poor circulation, movement, nail polish, cold extremities and skin pigmentation, so interpret values alongside the clinical picture.

radiation-protection-gloves.description: Radiation protection gloves are reusable gloves containing lead or lead-free attenuating materials such as tungsten, bismuth or antimony compounds, designed to reduce scattered radiation dose to the hands during fluoroscopy, interventional radiology, cardiac catheterization and orthopaedic imaging. These non-sterile gloves come in S to XL, from heavier gauntlet styles to thinner, more flexible types for tasks needing dexterity. They are intended for scattered radiation, so hands should still be kept out of the primary beam. Regular visual inspection for cracks and storage flat rather than folded help preserve the protective layer.

rehabilitation-steps.description: Rehabilitation steps are training stairs used in physiotherapy to practise stair climbing before discharge, after joint replacement, stroke, injury or prolonged illness. Units range from single or double step blocks to straight or corner staircases with handrails on both sides, and some allow step height to be adjusted as the patient progresses. Non-slip treads and a rigid, stable frame are essential for safety. Choose a design whose step height and handrail layout reflect the stairs the patient will face at home, and consider whether a top platform is needed for turning.
rehabilitation-steps.specifications: Configuration: single step, double step or staircase; Step height: adjustable or fixed; Treads: non-slip surface; Handrails: one or both sides (staircase models); Frame: wood or steel

resuscitation-kits.description: Resuscitation kits bring together the disposable supplies needed to manage airway and breathing during a cardiac or respiratory arrest. A typical kit includes a bag-valve-mask resuscitator with oxygen reservoir, face masks in several sizes, oropharyngeal airways, oxygen tubing and suction catheters, with some versions adding IV cannulas and syringes. Components are individually sterile-packed and grouped in a carry case or sealed pouch. Adult and paediatric configurations differ in bag, mask and airway size, so stock the correct kit for each care area and check expiry dates regularly.
resuscitation-kits.specifications: Configurations: adult and paediatric; Typical contents: BVM resuscitator, masks, oropharyngeal airways, oxygen tubing, suction catheters; Packaging: components individually sterile-packed; Container: carry bag, box or sealed pouch; Use: single-use consumables

retractors.description: Surgical retractors hold back skin, muscle and organs so the surgeon has a clear view of and access to the operative field. Hand-held types such as Langenbeck, Senn, Army-Navy and Deaver retractors are held by an assistant and repositioned as needed, while self-retaining types such as Weitlaner, Gelpi and Balfour retractors lock open with a ratchet or screw and free up staff. Blades come in different widths, depths and tip shapes, from smooth blades to sharp or blunt pronged rakes. Select blade depth and width for the incision, and use blunt blades near vessels and nerves.

safety-syringes.description: Safety syringes include a built-in mechanism that covers or withdraws the needle after injection to help prevent needlestick injuries and reuse. Retractable designs pull the needle into the barrel when the plunger is fully depressed, while shielded designs use a hinged or sliding sheath that locks over the needle. Auto-disable versions also lock the plunger after one use so the syringe cannot be refilled. Sizes typically range from 1mL to 10mL. Prefer mechanisms that activate one-handed and fit routine injection technique, and train staff before introduction.
safety-syringes.specifications: Sizes: 1–10mL; Mechanism: retractable needle, sliding or hinged shield, auto-disable; Activation: one-handed on many designs; Needle: attached, or luer fitting for separate safety needles; Packaging: sterile, single use

scalpel-handles.description: Scalpel handles are reusable stainless-steel holders that accept detachable, disposable surgical blades. The No.3 handle fits smaller blades such as No.10, 11, 12 and 15 for fine and general incisions, while the larger No.4 handle takes No.20 to 24 blades for longer incisions through thicker tissue. Long-shaft versions of the No.3 are available for deep cavities. Handles usually have a ribbed or knurled grip for control. Mount and remove blades with a needle holder or blade remover rather than fingers to reduce the risk of sharps injuries.

sharps-containers.description: Sharps containers are rigid, puncture-resistant, single-use boxes for disposing of used needles, scalpel blades, lancets and other sharps at the point of use. Typical sizes range from 0.5 L for trays and phlebotomy carts to 10 L for treatment rooms, with a restricted opening, needle-removal notches and a temporary closure for when the container is not in use. Once filled to the marked fill line, the lid is locked permanently for disposal. Choose sizes that can sit within arm's reach of where sharps are used, and mount or position containers so they stay upright and stable.

shoe-covers.description: Shoe covers are disposable overshoes that slip over footwear to limit tracking of dirt and contaminants into clean areas and to protect shoes from spills. They are made from polypropylene nonwoven, polyethylene film or CPE with an elasticated ankle opening, and some have a textured anti-skid sole for wet floors. They are used at entrances to operating theatres, ICUs, cleanrooms, laboratories and during home visits. Plain film covers can be slippery on smooth floors, so anti-skid versions are preferable where staff move quickly; for heavy fluid exposure, taller boot covers give better coverage.
shoe-covers.specifications: Material: PP nonwoven, PE or CPE film; Opening: elasticated ankle; Sole: plain or anti-skid textured; Size: one size, XL for large footwear; Sterility: non-sterile, single-use

spine-boards.description: Spine boards, or long backboards, are rigid flat boards used to move a patient with a suspected spinal injury while keeping the head, neck and trunk aligned. The patient is log-rolled onto the board and secured with straps and a head immobiliser. Modern boards are moulded polyethylene, X-ray translucent and often buoyant for water rescue, with multiple handholds and strap pins. Standard boards suit adults, with paediatric versions available. Boards are intended mainly for extrication and transfer, so time spent lying on one should be kept short.
spine-boards.specifications: Material: moulded high-density polyethylene; Length: standard adult, about 180–185cm; Paediatric: smaller boards available; Features: hand slots, strap pins, radiolucent; Compatibility: body straps and head immobiliser

splints.description: Splints immobilise suspected fractures, dislocations and soft-tissue injuries to reduce pain and prevent further damage during assessment and transport. Common types include mouldable foam-padded aluminium splints that can be shaped to any limb, rigid arm and leg boards, finger splints, and inflatable air splints that apply even pressure around the limb. Most are single-patient-use, though rigid versions can be cleaned and reused. Immobilise the joints above and below the injury, and check circulation, sensation and movement beyond the splint after applying it.
splints.specifications: Types: mouldable, rigid, inflatable, finger; Material: foam-padded aluminium, plastic or PVC; Sizes: arm, leg, finger, adult and paediatric; Fastening: hook-and-loop straps or bandage; Features: radiolucent options

steam-sterilizers.description: Steam sterilizers use saturated steam under pressure to kill microorganisms on heat- and moisture-tolerant medical devices and are the main sterilization method in most central sterile services departments. A typical cycle has an air-removal stage, often a series of vacuum pulses, followed by the sterilizing exposure and a drying phase so packs leave the chamber dry. Units range from small benchtop machines for wards and clinics to large floor-standing or pass-through sterilizers fed by the hospital steam supply or an integral generator. Daily air-removal testing, routine load monitoring and adequate water, power and drainage are central to reliable operation.

sterile-surgical-gloves.description: Sterile surgical gloves are single-use, individually packaged pairs for aseptic procedures where the glove will touch sterile instruments, open wounds or body cavities. Unlike examination gloves, they are sized by hand circumference in half sizes, here 5.5 to 8.5, and are anatomically shaped with long cuffs that overlap the gown sleeve. Beyond the operating theatre, they are used for bedside sterile tasks such as urinary catheter insertion, central line placement and wound procedures. The inner wrapper is folded so gloves can be put on without touching their outer surface; check that the pack is intact and in date before opening.

sterilization-containers.description: Sterilization containers are reusable rigid boxes, usually aluminium or high-temperature polymer, that hold instrument sets through sterilization, storage and transport to the operating room. Filters or valves in the lid, and sometimes the base, let steam in and out while maintaining a microbial barrier afterwards, and latching lids with tamper-evident seals show the set has not been opened. They come in half, three-quarter and full sizes to fit standard instrument baskets. Compared with disposable wraps they resist tearing and stack well, but gaskets, latches and filters need regular inspection, and cycles must be validated for rigid containers.
sterilization-containers.specifications: Material: anodized aluminium or high-temperature polymer; Barrier: disposable or long-life filters, or valve system; Sizes: half, three-quarter and full; Closure: latching lid with tamper-evident seal and label holder; Compatibility: steam, some models for low-temperature methods

sterilization-pouches.description: Sterilization pouches are self-sealing or heat-sealable packages with a transparent plastic film on one side and medical-grade paper on the other, used to package instruments so they can be sterilized and then kept sterile until use. Steam or gas penetrates through the paper while the film lets staff see the contents, and most carry printed process indicators that change colour after exposure. They come as flat pouches and gusseted or flat rolls, from about 65 x 100 mm up to 300 x 600 mm and rolls cut to length. Avoid overfilling, leave space around the item, and confirm the pouch type suits the sterilization method.
sterilization-pouches.specifications: Construction: medical-grade paper with laminated PET/PP film; Sealing: self-seal adhesive strip or heat seal; Formats: flat pouches, flat or gusseted rolls; Indicators: printed process indicators (steam and/or EO); Sizes: approx. 65 x 100 mm to 300 x 600 mm

sterilization-wraps.description: Sterilization wraps are flat sheets used to enclose instrument trays and linen packs before sterilization, letting the sterilant penetrate while forming a microbial barrier that keeps contents sterile during storage and transport. Disposable wraps are usually SMS polypropylene nonwoven or medical crepe paper, made in different weights for light to heavy trays. They are folded using envelope or square techniques, often in two layers, and secured with indicator tape. Sheets range from about 60 x 60 cm to 100 x 100 cm or larger; choose a size that allows complete coverage with overlapping folds and a weight that resists tearing at tray corners.
sterilization-wraps.specifications: Material: SMS polypropylene nonwoven or medical crepe paper; Weight: light to heavy grades, approx. 35–80 gsm; Sizes: approx. 60 x 60 cm to 100 x 100 cm and larger; Compatibility: steam and EO, PP wraps also for hydrogen peroxide plasma; Sterility: non-sterile until processed

supraglottic-airways.description: Supraglottic airways are a broad group of devices that sit above the vocal cords to allow ventilation without tracheal intubation, including second-generation designs with a gastric drain channel, non-inflatable gel cuffs and integrated bite blocks. They are used in anaesthesia, emergency and pre-hospital care, and resuscitation as a quick-to-insert airway when intubation is unnecessary or has failed, and some designs act as a conduit for passing an endotracheal tube. These sterile, single-use devices come in sizes 1 to 5, selected by patient weight. Designs with a drain tube give better protection against gastric inflation and regurgitation.
supraglottic-airways.specifications: Cuff type: inflatable or non-inflatable gel; Sizes: 1 (neonate) to 5 (large adult), weight-based; Features: gastric drain channel, bite block, 15 mm connector; Intubation conduit: on some designs; Sterility: sterile, single-use

suprapubic-catheters.description: Suprapubic catheters drain urine through a small opening in the lower abdomen directly into the bladder, bypassing the urethra. They are used for long-term drainage, urethral injury or obstruction, and when urethral catheters cause repeated problems. Most are silicone Foley-type catheters with a retention balloon, in sizes from 12Fr to 24Fr with various balloon capacities. Initial insertion is performed by trained clinicians, and later changes through the established tract are often done by nurses. Follow the manufacturer's guidance on maximum dwell time.

surface-disinfectants.description: Surface disinfectants are liquid solutions and pre-moistened wipes used to clean and disinfect environmental surfaces and non-critical equipment such as bed rails, trolleys, examination couches, countertops and monitors.
