Common active ingredients include alcohols, quaternary ammonium compounds, chlorine-releasing agents, hydrogen peroxide and blends, which differ in spectrum of activity, contact time and material compatibility. They are supplied in 500 mL to 5 L bottles and wipe tubs. When choosing, check activity against the organisms of concern, the wet contact time required, and compatibility with plastics and screens, as some agents damage materials with repeated use.
surface-disinfectants.specifications: Actives: alcohol, QAC, chlorine, hydrogen peroxide or blends; Format: ready-to-use liquid, concentrate or pre-saturated wipes; Pack sizes: 500 mL–5 L bottles, wipe tubs; Contact time: typically approx. 1–10 min, product-specific; Use: non-critical surfaces and equipment

surgical-blades.description: Surgical blades are sterile, single-use cutting edges made to fit standard scalpel handles, with blade shape determining their use. The No.10 has a curved edge for general skin incisions, the No.11 is a pointed triangular blade for stab incisions and drainage, the No.12 is hooked for suture removal and confined spaces, and the small curved No.15 gives precise, short cuts. The larger No.20 and 22 fit the No.4 handle for long incisions. Each blade is individually foil-packed and should be discarded straight into a sharps container after use.
surgical-blades.specifications: Material: carbon steel or stainless steel; Small blades: No.10, 11, 12, 15 for No.3 handle; Large blades: No.20, 22 and similar for No.4 handle; Packaging: individually foil-wrapped, sterile; Use: single use only

surgical-caps.description: Surgical caps are close-fitting head covers worn by surgeons and theatre staff to keep hair contained and reduce contamination of the surgical field. Common styles include the skull cap, which sits snugly with an elastic band at the back, and the tie-back surgeon's cap, which gives an adjustable, tailored fit; many include an absorbent sweatband across the forehead. Disposable versions are made from spunbond or SMS nonwoven, while reusable cotton caps are also used and must be laundered between uses. Staff with long hair may need a bouffant cap or hood instead, as close-fitting caps can leave hair exposed.
surgical-caps.specifications: Material: spunbond PP or SMS nonwoven (disposable), cotton or poly-cotton (reusable); Style: skull cap or tie-back surgeon's cap; Fastening: rear ties or elastic; Features: sweatband on some models; Sterility: non-sterile

surgical-clamps.description: Surgical clamps are locking instruments used to occlude, compress or hold vessels, bowel, ducts and other tissue during surgery, and to secure drapes or tubing. Many have longer or specially shaped jaws compared with fine hemostats, such as atraumatic intestinal clamps with longitudinal serrations, crushing clamps for tissue that will be resected, right-angle clamps for dissecting around structures, and towel clamps for draping. They are available straight or curved in various jaw lengths. Choose atraumatic jaws whenever the clamped tissue must remain viable after the clamp is removed.

surgical-forceps.description: Surgical forceps are instruments used to grasp, hold and manipulate tissue, dressings and swabs during operations and minor procedures. Thumb forceps, such as tissue and dressing forceps, are held like a pencil and work by spring tension; toothed tips give a secure grip on tougher tissue like skin, while non-toothed tips handle delicate tissue and vessels. Ring-handled forceps, such as artery and sponge-holding forceps, lock with a ratchet to clamp or hold. They range from about 10 to 25 cm in stainless steel for reprocessing between uses. Inspect tips for alignment and wear, as damaged teeth can crush or slip on tissue.

surgical-gowns.description: Surgical gowns are sterile gowns worn by the scrub team to maintain the sterile field and act as a barrier against blood and fluid strike-through during operations. The front and sleeves are the critical zones, so many designs add reinforced, fluid-impervious panels there, with knitted cuffs that sit under the glove cuff and a wrap-around back closed with a tie card. Most are single-use SMS or spunlace nonwovens, though reusable woven fabric variants exist. Sizes run S to XL; choose reinforcement and fluid resistance according to the expected length of the procedure and volume of fluid.
surgical-gowns.specifications: Material: SMS, spunlace or laminated nonwoven; Reinforcement: standard or reinforced front and sleeves; Cuffs: knitted; Closure: wrap-around back with neck fastening and tie card; Sterility: sterile, individually packed

surgical-masks.description: Surgical masks are loose-fitting, disposable face masks worn to protect patients and the sterile field from the wearer's respiratory droplets and to shield the wearer's nose and mouth from splashes. They usually have three layers: a fluid-resistant outer nonwoven, a melt-blown filter layer and a soft inner layer, with a bendable nose wire and either ear loops or tie-on straps. Tie-on styles are common in operating rooms, ear-loop styles on wards and in clinics, and paediatric sizes are available alongside the adult one-size. Because they do not seal to the face, they are not a substitute for a fitted respirator against airborne particles.

surgical-scissors.description: Surgical scissors are precision cutting instruments for cutting tissue, sutures, dressings and other materials during operations and minor procedures. Common patterns include Metzenbaum scissors for delicate tissue dissection, Mayo scissors for heavier tissue and fascia, iris scissors for fine work and suture scissors for stitches, in straight or curved forms and lengths of about 11 to 23 cm. Tips may be sharp/sharp, sharp/blunt or blunt/blunt, and tungsten carbide inserts help blades stay sharp longer. Reusable stainless steel scissors are cleaned and sterilized between uses and should be inspected for sharpness and alignment; sterile single-use versions are also available.

surgical-suction-units.description: Surgical suction units generate high vacuum to remove blood, irrigation fluid and debris from the operative field so the surgeon keeps a clear view. Mobile units have a built-in pump on a wheeled base, while wall-mounted regulators connect to the hospital's central vacuum supply. Fluid collects in canisters or disposable liners fitted with an overflow shut-off and filter, and suction is delivered through sterile tubing and Yankauer or Poole tips. Check vacuum level, flow rate and canister capacity, and keep a portable backup where wall suction may fail.
surgical-suction-units.specifications: Type: mobile pump unit or wall vacuum regulator; Vacuum: adjustable high-vacuum with gauge; Collection: reusable canisters or disposable liners; Protection: overflow valve and filter; Power: mains, battery on some portable units

syringe-pumps.description: Syringe pumps drive the plunger of a loaded syringe at a precise, steady rate, making them suited to small-volume, high-concentration infusions such as vasopressors, sedation, insulin and neonatal medicines. They accept standard syringes of about 5mL to 60mL and deliver rates typically from 0.1 to 1200 mL/h, with bolus, purge and occlusion alarm functions. The syringe size and type must be correctly set or recognised for accurate delivery. Check which syringe brands and sizes are calibrated on the pump before standardising supplies.

tablet-counters.description: Tablet counters help pharmacy staff count tablets and capsules accurately and hygienically when dispensing. Manual counting trays have a raised counting area, a spatula and a channel or spout that returns excess tablets to the stock bottle, while electronic counters use optical sensors or weighing to count units as they are poured or fed through. Electronic models speed up high-volume dispensing and reduce miscounts. Counting surfaces should be cleaned between medicines to prevent cross-contamination, and dedicated trays are often kept for cytotoxic drugs or allergens such as penicillins.
tablet-counters.specifications: Types: manual tray or electronic counter; Manual design: tray with spatula and return spout; Electronic counting: optical sensor or weight-based; Material: plastic or stainless steel; Cleaning: wipe-clean counting surfaces

tens-units.description: TENS (transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation) units are small, battery-powered stimulators that deliver mild electrical pulses through skin electrodes to help relieve acute and chronic pain. Portable units commonly have two to four channels with adjustable intensity, pulse rate and pulse width, plus preset programmes such as conventional, burst and modulated modes. They are used in physiotherapy departments and for home pain management, with self-adhesive electrode pads replaced as their adhesion wears. Units with simple controls and clearly labelled presets suit home users, while clinicians may prefer fully adjustable parameters.
tens-units.specifications: Channels: 2–4; Pulse rate: approx. 1–150 Hz; Pulse width: approx. 50–300 µs; Modes: conventional, burst, modulated; Power: disposable or rechargeable batteries; Electrodes: self-adhesive pads

thermal-heat-resistant-gloves.description: Thermal or heat-resistant gloves are reusable insulating gloves for safely handling hot items, such as loads removed from autoclaves and dry heat sterilizers, glassware from laboratory ovens, and equipment from hotplates or water baths. They are typically made from aramid or similar heat-resistant fibres, silicone-coated fabric or insulated cotton, often with a long gauntlet cuff to protect the wrist and forearm, in sizes S to XL. Check the rated contact temperature against the task, and note that fabric gloves insulate poorly once wet, so steam-heavy work may call for a silicone or water-resistant outer surface.

tongue-depressors.description: Tongue depressors are flat, smooth wooden blades used to hold down the tongue during examination of the mouth and throat, and also serve as simple finger splints and spatulas for mixing or applying ointments. Adult blades are about 15cm long, with shorter, narrower paediatric versions for children. They are made from smooth, splinter-free hardwood such as birch. Non-sterile blades are common for routine examinations, while individually wrapped sterile blades suit procedures and higher-risk settings. Each blade is discarded after a single use.
tongue-depressors.specifications: Material: smooth hardwood, commonly birch; Adult size: about 150 x 18mm; Paediatric: shorter, narrower blade; Packaging: bulk boxes or individually wrapped; Sterility: non-sterile, sterile options

tracheostomy-tubes.description: Tracheostomy tubes are curved tubes inserted through a surgical or percutaneous opening in the front of the neck into the trachea, used for prolonged ventilation, upper airway obstruction, secretion management and weaning from a ventilator. They come cuffed or uncuffed, with or without a removable inner cannula for cleaning, and in fenestrated versions that can allow speech when appropriate, with a neck flange and ties holding the tube in place. Most are sterile single-use PVC or silicone tubes from neonatal to adult sizes, with some reusable metal variants. Sizing should consider both internal diameter and length to suit neck anatomy.
tracheostomy-tubes.specifications: Material: PVC or silicone, some reusable metal; Sizes: neonatal to adult, by ID and length; Cuff: cuffed or uncuffed; Options: inner cannula, fenestration, adjustable flange, extended length; Sterility: sterile, packed with obturator

trauma-kits.description: Trauma kits assemble the supplies needed to control bleeding and manage injuries at the scene, in transit or in the emergency department. Contents commonly include tourniquets, pressure and haemostatic dressings, trauma bandages, gauze, shears, gloves, chest seals and airway adjuncts, with components individually sterile-packed where required. Sizes range from compact individual first-responder pouches to large bags stocked for multiple casualties. Choose a kit by the number of patients and the injury types expected, and log used or expiring items so they are replaced.
trauma-kits.specifications: Sizes: individual, team and mass-casualty; Typical contents: tourniquet, trauma dressings, gauze, chest seal, shears, gloves; Packaging: components individually sterile-packed; Case: pouch, backpack or hard case with compartments; Use: consumables single use

ultrasound-machines.description: Cart-based ultrasound machines are full-size diagnostic scanners used in radiology and imaging departments for abdominal, obstetric, vascular, cardiac, musculoskeletal and small-parts examinations. A processing unit, large monitor and control panel sit on a wheeled cart with several transducer ports, so linear, convex, phased-array and endocavity probes can stay connected. Imaging modes typically include B-mode, M-mode and colour and spectral Doppler, with advanced software options on some systems. Match the probe set and software packages to the department's examination mix, and confirm image storage and PACS connectivity.

ultrasound-printers.description: Ultrasound printers are compact thermal video printers that produce instant hard-copy images from ultrasound scanners, commonly used for obstetric pictures, report attachments and patient files. They connect to the scanner by video or USB output and print in black-and-white on thermal paper, with some colour models using dedicated media. Most are small enough to mount on the ultrasound cart. Selection depends on the scanner's output connections, required print size and paper type, and the running cost of thermal paper, especially where departments rely mainly on digital storage and print only on request.
ultrasound-printers.specifications: Print type: thermal, monochrome (colour variants available); Paper: thermal roll, commonly 110 mm wide; Connection: analogue video and/or USB; Media: standard or high-density/glossy thermal paper; Mounting: on-cart or desktop

ultrasound-probes.description: Ultrasound probes (transducers) convert electrical signals into sound waves and back, and the probe type largely determines what a system can image. Linear probes use higher frequencies for superficial structures such as vessels, thyroid and musculoskeletal tissue; convex probes use lower frequencies for abdominal and obstetric scans; phased-array probes have a small footprint for cardiac imaging between the ribs; and endocavity probes are used for transvaginal and transrectal examinations. Probes must be compatible with the specific ultrasound system, and invasive use requires a sterile cover and appropriate disinfection between patients.
ultrasound-probes.specifications: Types: linear, convex, phased-array, endocavity; Linear frequency: approx. 5–15 MHz; Convex frequency: approx. 2–6 MHz; Phased-array frequency: approx. 1–5 MHz; Endocavity frequency: approx. 4–10 MHz; Compatibility: system-specific connector

ultrasound-therapy-machines.description: Therapeutic ultrasound machines deliver high-frequency sound waves through a treatment head to heat and stimulate soft tissue, used in physiotherapy for musculoskeletal conditions such as tendinopathy, sprains and joint stiffness. Most have interchangeable heads at 1 MHz for deeper tissues and 3 MHz for more superficial structures, with continuous or pulsed output, adjustable intensity and a timer. Unlike diagnostic scanners, they do not produce images. Coupling gel is required and the head is kept moving during treatment; consider available head sizes and whether output can be checked periodically.
ultrasound-therapy-machines.specifications: Frequency: 1 MHz and 3 MHz; Output mode: continuous or pulsed; Intensity: adjustable, up to approx. 2–3 W/cm²; Treatment heads: small and large, approx. 1 cm² and 5 cm²; Timer: adjustable treatment time

urine-analyzers.description: Urine analyzers are benchtop instruments that read urine reagent strips automatically by reflectance photometry, removing the subjectivity of judging colour changes by eye. A dipped strip is placed on the tray and the analyzer reports parameters such as glucose, protein, blood, leukocytes, nitrite, ketones, pH and specific gravity, then prints or stores the result. They are used in outpatient clinics, wards and laboratories for routine urinalysis and screening. Each analyzer reads only compatible strip types, so check ongoing strip supply and cost, and follow the dipping, blotting and timing steps exactly for consistent results.
urine-analyzers.specifications: Method: reflectance photometry; Parameters: up to approx. 10–14 per strip; Throughput: dozens to several hundred strips per hour; Output: built-in printer, USB or LIS connection on many models; Consumables: compatible reagent strips, calibration strips

urine-bags.description: Urine bags collect urine from an indwelling catheter in a closed drainage system. Bedside bags hold about 750mL to 2000mL and hang from the bed frame on a hanger, and are available with an outlet tap for emptying without disconnecting the system or without a tap for single fill-and-discard use. Common features include a non-return valve to prevent backflow, printed volume graduations and, on some models, a sampling port. Keep the bag below bladder level and off the floor, and empty it before it becomes full.
urine-bags.specifications: Capacity: 750–2000mL; Outlet: with or without drain tap; Valve: non-return anti-reflux; Graduations: printed volume markings; Fluid path: sterile, single use

urine-collection-containers.description: Urine collection containers are screw-cap specimen pots and larger jugs used to collect and transport urine for laboratory analysis. Sterile 60 mL and 120 mL containers are used for midstream and culture samples, non-sterile versions suit routine urinalysis, and 2–3 L containers are used for 24-hour collections for tests such as creatinine clearance or urine protein. Containers usually have a leak-resistant cap, graduated markings and a label area for patient details. Use a sterile container whenever a culture is requested, and check whether a 24-hour test requires a container with preservative added.
urine-collection-containers.specifications: Capacity: 60 mL, 120 mL, 2–3 L (24-hour); Material: polypropylene or polystyrene; Closure: leak-resistant screw cap; Markings: graduated scale with label area; Sterility: sterile or non-sterile variants

urine-drainage-sets.description: Urine drainage sets connect to an indwelling catheter to form a closed drainage system, carrying urine through tubing into a collection bag kept below bladder level. Bedside configurations typically use a 1.5–2 L bag with a long drainage tube, bed hanger and bottom outlet tap, while leg-bag configurations suit ambulant patients. Features such as a non-return valve, needle-free sampling port and graduated volume markings support infection control and output monitoring. Keeping the system closed and the bag below the bladder helps reduce the risk of catheter-associated urinary tract infection.
urine-drainage-sets.specifications: Bag capacity: typically 1.5–2 L (bedside); Tubing: kink-resistant drainage tube; Valve: non-return anti-reflux; Sampling port: needle-free; Outlet: bottom drain tap; Accessories: bed hanger or leg straps

uv-sterilization-cabinets.description: UV sterilization cabinets are enclosed units that expose items to ultraviolet-C light to reduce microbial contamination on the surfaces of objects such as stethoscopes, phones, tablets, keyboards, clean instruments in storage and other small reusable items. They range from small benchtop cabinets to walk-in units, and typically combine UV-C lamps with a cycle timer, door safety interlock and reflective interior. UV acts only where light reaches directly, so shadowed areas, crevices and soiled surfaces are not reliably treated. These cabinets disinfect surfaces and do not replace steam or other validated sterilization of critical devices.
uv-sterilization-cabinets.specifications: UV source: low-pressure mercury or LED UV-C lamps; Wavelength: approx. 254 nm (mercury), approx. 260–280 nm (LED); Controls: cycle timer, door safety interlock; Interior: stainless steel or reflective lining with shelves or racks; Capacity: benchtop cabinet to walk-in unit

vaccine-refrigerators.description: Vaccine refrigerators keep vaccines within the 2–8°C range needed to preserve potency, with tighter temperature stability and protection than general-purpose units. Types include mains-powered upright or chest units, ice-lined models that hold temperature through power cuts, and solar direct-drive units for sites with unreliable electricity, which suits immunisation clinics and remote facilities. Typical capacities are about 100 L to 300 L. Continuous temperature monitoring with a data logger, freeze protection and an organised storage layout help prevent freezing, which can irreversibly damage many vaccines.

vaginal-speculums.description: Vaginal speculums gently open the vaginal walls to give a clear view of the cervix for examination, cervical screening, IUD insertion and other procedures. Graves speculums have wider, curved blades suited to multiparous patients, while Pederson speculums have narrower, flatter blades for nulliparous or postmenopausal patients; both come in small, medium and large. Disposable plastic speculums are supplied sterile and some accept an attachable light source, while reusable stainless steel versions are reprocessed between patients. Choosing the smallest size that gives an adequate view improves patient comfort.
vaginal-speculums.specifications: Types: Graves and Pederson; Sizes: small, medium, large; Material: clear plastic or stainless steel; Blade locking: ratchet or screw adjustment; Options: light source attachment (plastic types)

ventilators.description: Ventilators are machines that mechanically move air and oxygen into and out of the lungs for patients who cannot breathe adequately on their own, either through an endotracheal or tracheostomy tube or non-invasively with a mask. ICU ventilators offer a full range of volume, pressure and spontaneous modes with detailed monitoring, while transport and portable units are smaller, battery-powered and suited to transfers and emergencies. Adult, paediatric and neonatal capability depends on the model. Selection should consider the patient population, required modes, gas supply, battery runtime and the availability of compatible circuits, filters and humidifiers.

walking-frames.description: Walking frames are lightweight four-legged mobility aids that give users a wide, stable base of support, used in rehabilitation after surgery, falls or illness and for long-term mobility. Standard frames are lifted and moved forward with each step, while front-wheeled frames are pushed for a smoother gait, and folding models aid transport and storage. Height-adjustable legs allow fitting, and bariatric frames offer higher weight capacity. The handgrips are usually set at wrist height with the user standing upright, and rubber ferrules should be checked regularly for wear.
walking-frames.specifications: Frame: aluminium or steel; Types: standard, front-wheeled, folding, bariatric; Height: adjustable push-button legs; Weight capacity: standard and bariatric ratings; Tips: rubber ferrules or front castors

wall-mounted-bp-monitors.description: Wall-mounted BP monitors are fixed blood pressure units installed in examination rooms, triage bays and ward areas, keeping the gauge at eye level and the cuff always at hand. Most are aneroid units with a large dial on a wall bracket, a coiled tube and a basket to hold the cuff, though digital wall-mounted models also exist. Because they cannot be dropped or misplaced, they tend to hold calibration longer and save bench space in busy rooms. Mount them at a convenient height beside the examination couch and check that the tubing reaches the patient's arm both sitting and lying.
wall-mounted-bp-monitors.specifications: Type: aneroid dial, digital models available; Scale: 0–300 mmHg; Dial: large face for reading at a distance; Mounting: wall bracket with cuff basket and coiled tubing; Cuffs: adult, large adult

waste-segregation-bins.description: Waste segregation bins are colour-coded sets of bins placed side by side so staff can separate healthcare waste where it is produced into categories such as infectious, general, recyclable and pharmaceutical waste. Each bin is labelled with its colour, symbol and accepted items, and sets may be freestanding, held in a shared frame or mounted on a trolley. Capacities can be mixed to match how much of each waste type an area generates. Segregating at source reduces the volume of waste needing costly treatment, and the colour scheme should follow local waste management rules.

wheelchairs.description: Wheelchairs move patients who cannot walk, or should not walk, between wards, clinics, imaging and discharge areas. Self-propelled chairs have large rear wheels with push rims, while attendant-propelled transit chairs use small wheels and rely on a porter or carer. Frames are steel for durability or aluminium for lighter lifting, in folding or rigid designs, with widths from paediatric and narrow to standard and bariatric and weight capacity of roughly 100kg to 200kg. Check for swing-away footrests and removable armrests to ease transfers, and reliable parking brakes.

wound-care-kits.description: Wound care kits are more complete packs than basic dressing sets, grouping cleansing, closure and dressing supplies for a specific task such as suture removal, laceration care, burns or chronic wound care. Basic kits may contain gauze, antiseptic, adhesive dressings and tape, while advanced kits add sterile instruments, saline, specialised dressings and gloves. Components are individually sterile-packed so unused items stay clean. Kits suit wards, outpatient clinics, community nursing and home care; choose the configuration that matches the wound types most often treated.
wound-care-kits.specifications: Configurations: basic to advanced; Typical contents: gauze, saline or antiseptic, dressings, tape, gloves, instruments; Packaging: components individually sterile-packed; Container: pouch or box; Use: single use

wound-irrigation-systems.description: Wound irrigation systems deliver a steady stream of saline or another solution to flush debris, bacteria and loose tissue from wounds and lacerations before closure or dressing. Options range from pressurised single-use saline cans and squeeze bottles to syringe-based kits and reusable pressure devices with disposable splash-guard tips. Effective cleansing generally uses moderate pressure, roughly 4 to 15 psi, enough to remove contaminants without driving them deeper into tissue. Volumes typically run from 100mL to 1000mL depending on wound size, and splash shields protect staff from contaminated spray.
wound-irrigation-systems.specifications: Types: pressurised can, squeeze bottle, syringe kit, reusable pressure device; Pressure: about 4–15 psi; Volume: typically 100–1000mL; Tips: disposable, with splash shield; Fluid path: sterile

x-ray-accessories.description: X-ray accessories are the supporting items that make radiography safe and effective, including anti-scatter grids, cassettes, lead aprons and thyroid shields, and positioning or anatomical markers. Grids improve image contrast by absorbing scattered radiation, cassettes hold film or imaging plates, and lead-equivalent garments shield staff and patients from unnecessary exposure, while left and right markers identify orientation on the image. Choose cassette and grid sizes to match the equipment in use, select apron lead equivalence and fit according to the tasks performed, and inspect protective garments periodically for cracks.
